title.zh: 卷二百八十一 列傳第四十 呂端 畢士安曾孫:仲衍 仲游 寇準
title.en: Volume 281 Biographies 40: Lu Duan, Bi Shiancengsun:Zhongyan, Zhong You, Kou Zhun
title.raw: 卷二百八十一 列傳第四十 呂端 畢士安曾孫:仲衍 仲游 寇準 Volume 281 Biographies 40: Lu Duan, Bi Shiancengsun:Zhongyan, Zhong You, Kou Zhun

sentences.zh: 呂端，字易直，幽州安次人。

translations.literal: Lü Duan, courtesy name Yizhi, was a native of Anci in You Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Duan, styled Yizhi, came from Anci in You Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父琦，晉兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: His father Qi was Vice Minister of War under Jin.
translations.idiomatic: His father Qi had been Vice Minister of War under Jin.

sentences.zh: 端少敏悟好學，以蔭補千牛備身。

translations.literal: Duan from youth was perceptive and fond of learning; by hereditary privilege he was appointed Imperial Guard Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Lu Duan was quick and studious; by hereditary privilege he entered service as an imperial guard attendant.

sentences.zh: 歷國子主簿、太僕寺丞、秘書郎、直弘文館，換著作佐郎、直史館。

translations.literal: He served as registrar of the Directorate of Education, vice director of the Court of the Imperial Stud, secretary, and attendant of the Hongwen Hall; he transferred to assistant editorial director and attendant of the Historiography Institute.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through registrar of the Directorate of Education, vice director of the Court of the Imperial Stud, secretary, and Hongwen Hall attendant, then transferred to assistant editorial director and historiography attendant.

sentences.zh: 太祖即位，遷太常丞、知浚儀縣，同判定州。

translations.literal: When Taizu acceded, he was promoted to vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and magistrate of Junyi county, and concurrently judged Ding Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: At Taizu's accession he was made vice director of sacrifices, magistrate of Junyi county, and concurrent judge of Ding Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 開寶中，西上閤門使郝崇信使契丹，以端假太常少卿為副。

translations.literal: During Kaibao, Western Upper Gate Commissioner Hao Chongxin was envoy to the Khitan; Duan served as acting vice director of sacrifices as his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaibao, when Western Upper Gate Commissioner Hao Chongxin went as envoy to the Khitan, Lu Duan served as acting sacrifices vice director on his staff.

sentences.zh: 八年，知洪州，未上，改司門員外郎、知成都府，賜金紫。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was appointed prefect of Hong but did not take up the post; he was changed to vice director of the Ministry of Justice and made prefect of Chengdu, and granted gold and purple insignia.
translations.idiomatic: In year eight he was named prefect of Hong but never took up the post; reassigned as justice vice director and prefect of Chengdu, with gold and purple insignia.

sentences.zh: 為政清簡，遠人便之。

translations.literal: His governance was clear and simple, and distant people found it convenient.
translations.idiomatic: His rule was spare and clear, to the comfort of the frontier population.

sentences.zh: 會秦王廷美尹京，召拜考功員外郎，充開封府判官。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Qin Tingmei was administering the capital, [Lu Duan] was summoned and appointed Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel, and served as judge of the Kaifeng prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince of Qin Zhao Tingmei was put in charge of the capital, Lu Duan was summoned and appointed Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel, serving as administrative judge of Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 太宗征河東，廷美將有居留之命，端白廷美曰：「主上櫛風沐雨，以申吊伐，王地處親賢，當表率扈從。

translations.literal: When Emperor Taizong campaigned in Hedong, Tingmei was about to receive orders to remain behind; Duan told Tingmei, saying: "The lord endures wind and rain to proclaim consolation and punitive expedition; the Prince, occupying a position among kin and worthies, ought to lead and follow in attendance.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taizong campaigned against Hedong, Tingmei was slated to stay behind; Lu Duan urged him: "The Emperor is braving wind and rain on a punitive expedition to right wrongs. As a prince among the imperial kin, you ought to set the example and march in his train.

sentences.zh: 今主留務，非所宜也。」

translations.literal: For the lord now to remain and handle affairs is not fitting."
translations.idiomatic: For you to stay behind and manage affairs now would be inappropriate."

sentences.zh: 廷美由是懇請從行。

translations.literal: Thereupon Tingmei earnestly requested to accompany the campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Tingmei thereupon begged permission to join the expedition.

sentences.zh: 尋坐王府親吏請托執事者違詔市竹木，貶商州司戶參軍。

translations.literal: Soon afterward, because a close clerk of the prince's establishment had solicited favors of officials and violated an edict by trading bamboo and lumber, [he] was demoted to military aide in Shang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after, he was demoted to Registrar of Shang Prefecture when a household clerk of the prince's establishment was found to have solicited favors from officials and illegally traded bamboo and timber in violation of an edict.

sentences.zh: 移汝州，復為太常丞、判寺事。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Ru Prefecture, and again made Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, judging its affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Ru Prefecture and then reappointed Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, with responsibility for its administration.

sentences.zh: 出知蔡州，以善政，吏民列奏借留。

translations.literal: He went out to serve as prefect of Cai; because of good governance, officials and people jointly memorialized requesting that he be retained.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted as prefect of Cai. His effective rule led local officials and the populace to petition collectively asking that he be kept in office.

sentences.zh: 改祠部員外郎、知開封縣，遷考功員外郎兼侍御史知雜事。

translations.literal: He was changed to Vice Director of the Ministry of Rites and magistrate of Kaifeng county, and promoted to Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel while concurrently serving as Attending Censor with charge of miscellaneous matters.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned as Vice Director of the Ministry of Rites and magistrate of Kaifeng county, then promoted to Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel and Attending Censor with general supervisory duties.

sentences.zh: 使高麗，暴風折檣，舟人怖恐，端讀書若在齋閣時。

translations.literal: On a mission to Goryeo, a violent wind broke the mast; the boatmen were terrified, yet Duan read books as if he were in his study hall.
translations.idiomatic: While envoy to Goryeo, a violent storm snapped the mast and terrified the crew, but Lu Duan read on as calmly as if he were in his private study.

sentences.zh: 遷戶部郎中、判太常寺兼禮院，選為大理少卿，俄拜右諫議大夫。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Director in the Ministry of Revenue, judged the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and concurrently the Office of Rites, was selected as Vice Director of the Court of Judicial Review, and soon received appointment as Right Remonstrance Grandee.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Director in the Ministry of Revenue, adjudicated at the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and the Office of Rites, was chosen Vice Director of the Court of Judicial Review, and soon appointed Right Remonstrance Grandee.

sentences.zh: 許王元僖尹開封，又為判官。

translations.literal: Prince of Xu Yuanxi was metropolitan governor of Kaifeng, and [Duan] again served as his administrative judge.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuanxi, Prince of Xu, governed Kaifeng, Lu Duan again served as his administrative judge.

sentences.zh: 王薨，有發其陰事者，坐裨贊無狀，遣御史武元穎、內侍王繼恩就鞫於府。

translations.literal: When the prince died, someone exposed his secret misconduct; for improper counsel he was sentenced, and Censor Wu Yuanying and inner attendant Wang Jien were sent to interrogate him at the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After the prince's death, secret misconduct was exposed; blamed for improper counsel, Lu Duan was investigated on the spot by Censor Wu Yuanying and inner attendant Wang Jien at the prefectural office.

sentences.zh: 端方決事，徐起候之，二使曰：「有詔推君。」

translations.literal: Duan was in the midst of deciding a case when he rose slowly to receive them; the two envoys said: "There is an edict to investigate you."
translations.idiomatic: Lu Duan was in the midst of deciding a case when he rose slowly to receive them. The two envoys said, "There is an edict to investigate you."

sentences.zh: 端神色自若，顧從者曰：「取帽來。」

translations.literal: Duan's expression remained calm; he turned to an attendant and said: "Bring my hat."
translations.idiomatic: His expression remained calm. He turned to an attendant and said, "Bring my hat."

sentences.zh: 二使曰：「何遽至此？」

translations.literal: The two envoys said: "Why so sudden?"
translations.idiomatic: The two envoys said, "Why so sudden?"

sentences.zh: 端曰：「天子有制問，即罪人矣，安可在堂上對制使？」

translations.literal: Duan said: "When the Son of Heaven has an imperial inquiry, one is already a guilty man — how can one face the inquiry commissioner in the hall?"
translations.idiomatic: Lu Duan said, "When the Son of Heaven has an imperial inquiry, one is already a guilty man — how can one face the inquiry commissioner in the hall?"

sentences.zh: 即下堂，隨問而答。

translations.literal: He went down from the hall at once and answered as questioned.
translations.idiomatic: He went down from the hall at once and answered as questioned.

sentences.zh: 左遷衛尉少卿。

translations.literal: He was demoted to vice director of the Court of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: He was demoted to vice director of the Court of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 會置考課院，群官有負譴置散秩者，引對，皆泣涕，以饑寒為請。

translations.literal: When the Performance Review Office was established, officials who had been censured and placed in nominal ranks were summoned for audience; all wept and pleaded poverty and hunger.
translations.idiomatic: When the Performance Review Office was set up, demoted officials in nominal posts were called to audience; all wept and begged relief from hunger and cold.

sentences.zh: 至端，即奏曰：「臣前佐秦邸，以不檢府吏，謫掾商州，陛下復擢官籍辱用。

translations.literal: When it came to Duan, he memorialized at once: "I formerly served the Prince of Qin's establishment and, for failing to restrain household clerks, was demoted to registrar in Shang Prefecture; Your Majesty then restored me to the rolls and honored me with employment.
translations.idiomatic: When it came to Lu Duan, he memorialized at once: "I formerly served the Prince of Qin's establishment and, for failing to restrain household clerks, was demoted to registrar in Shang Prefecture. Your Majesty then restored me to the rolls and honored me with employment.

sentences.zh: 今許王暴薨，臣輔佐無狀，陛下又不重譴，俾亞少列，臣罪大而幸深矣！

translations.literal: Now Prince of Xu died suddenly; my assistance was unworthy, yet Your Majesty did not punish me severely, placing me among the junior ranks — my offense is great and my fortune deep!
translations.idiomatic: Now Prince of Xu died suddenly; my assistance was unworthy, yet Your Majesty did not punish me severely, placing me among the junior ranks — my offense is great and my fortune deep!

sentences.zh: 今有司進退善否，苟得潁州副使，臣之願也。」

translations.literal: Now the authorities judge merit and fault; if I might receive the deputy regimentation commissionership of Ying Prefecture, that is my wish."
translations.idiomatic: Now the authorities judge merit and fault; if I might receive the deputy regimentation commissionership of Ying Prefecture, that is my wish."

sentences.zh: 太宗曰：「朕自知卿。」

translations.literal: Taizong said: "I know you myself."
translations.idiomatic: Taizong said, "I know you myself."

sentences.zh: 無何，復舊官，為樞密直學士，逾月，拜參知政事。

translations.literal: Before long he was restored to his former office, made Academician Directly Attached to the Bureau of Military Affairs, and after a month appointed Participant in Governance.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was restored to his former office, made Academician Directly Attached to the Bureau of Military Affairs, and after a month appointed Participant in Governance.

sentences.zh: 時趙普在中書，嘗曰：「吾觀呂公奏事，得嘉賞未嘗喜，遇抑挫未嘗懼，亦不形於言，真台輔之器也。」

translations.literal: At the time Zhao Pu was in the Secretariat; he once said: "When I observe Lord Lu memorializing, upon receiving commendation he has never shown joy, and upon meeting setbacks he has never shown fear; nor does he reveal it in words — truly the material of a chief minister."
translations.idiomatic: While Zhao Pu served in the Secretariat, he remarked: "I have watched Lord Lu present memorials. Praise never elates him, setbacks never frighten him, and he never betrays either in his words — he is truly fit for the highest office."

sentences.zh: 歲餘，左諫議大夫寇準亦拜參知政事。

translations.literal: More than a year later, Left Remonstrance Grandee Kou Zhun also received appointment as Participant in Governance.
translations.idiomatic: A year later, Kou Zhun, Left Remonstrance Grandee, was also appointed Participant in Governance.

sentences.zh: 端請居準下，太宗即以端為左諫議大夫，立準上。

translations.literal: Duan requested to rank below Kou; the Emperor thereupon made Duan Left Remonstrance Grandee, placing him above Kou.
translations.idiomatic: Duan asked to rank below Kou Zhun, but the Emperor made him Left Remonstrance Grandee instead, placing him above Kou.

sentences.zh: 每獨召便殿，語必移晷。

translations.literal: Whenever he was summoned alone to the Hall of Convenience, their talks always lasted until the sundial had moved far.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the Emperor summoned him alone to the Hall of Convenience, their conversations always ran until the sundial had shifted markedly.

sentences.zh: 擢拜戶部侍郎、平章事。

translations.literal: He was promoted and appointed Vice Minister of Revenue and Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Vice Minister of Revenue and appointed Grand Councillor.

sentences.zh: 時呂蒙正為相，太宗欲相端，或曰：「端為人糊塗。」

translations.literal: At the time Lü Mengzheng was chief minister; the Emperor wished to make Duan chief minister, but some said: "Duan is muddle-headed in his ways."
translations.idiomatic: Lü Mengzheng was then chief minister. When the Emperor wished to appoint Lu Duan in his place, some objected that "Duan is hopelessly absent-minded."

sentences.zh: 太宗曰：「端小事糊塗，大事不糊塗。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Duan is muddle-headed in small matters, but not in great affairs."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor replied: "He may be absent-minded in small matters, but not in great ones."

sentences.zh: 決意相之。

translations.literal: He resolved to appoint him chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: With that, he resolved to make him chief minister.

sentences.zh: 會曲宴後苑，太宗作《釣魚詩》，有云：「欲餌金鉤深未達，磻溪須問釣魚人。」

translations.literal: At a private banquet in the rear garden, the Emperor composed "Fishing," with a line: "The golden hook's depth I have not yet reached — at Pan Brook one must ask the fisherman."
translations.idiomatic: At a private banquet in the rear garden, the Emperor composed "Fishing," which included the lines: "The golden hook has not yet reached the depths I seek — at Pan Brook one must ask the fisherman."

sentences.zh: 意以屬端。

translations.literal: The meaning was to single out Duan.
translations.idiomatic: The poem was meant to point to Lu Duan.

sentences.zh: 後數日，罷蒙正而相端焉。

translations.literal: Several days later, Mengzheng was dismissed and Duan was made chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: A few days later, Lü Mengzheng was dismissed and Lu Duan was made chief minister.

sentences.zh: 初，端兄餘慶，建隆中以藩府舊僚參預大政，端復居相位，時論榮之。

translations.literal: Initially, Duan's elder brother Yuqing had in the Jianlong era, as an old follower of the prince's establishment, joined in great governance; now Duan again held the chief ministership — contemporaries honored this.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Duan's elder brother Yuqing had risen to high office in the Jianlong era as a veteran of the prince's household; now Duan too held the chief ministership, and contemporaries regarded the family with admiration.

sentences.zh: 端歷官僅四十年，至是驟被獎擢，太宗猶恨任用之晚。

translations.literal: Duan had held office for barely forty years; only now was he suddenly rewarded with promotion, and the Emperor still regretted that his appointment had come late.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Duan had served in office for nearly forty years before this sudden elevation, and the Emperor still felt he had been promoted too late.

sentences.zh: 端為相持重，識大體，以清簡為務。

translations.literal: As chief minister Duan was steady and grasped the larger pattern, making simplicity and restraint his task.
translations.idiomatic: As chief minister he was grave and steady, grasped the larger pattern, and made simplicity and restraint his guiding principles.

sentences.zh: 慮與寇準同列，先居相位，恐準不平，乃請參知政事與宰相分日押班知印，同升政事堂，太宗從之。

translations.literal: Concerned that serving together with Kou Zhun, he having first held the chief ministership might displease Kou, he requested that Participants in Governance and the chief minister take turns supervising the seal on alternate days and ascend the Hall of Administration together; the Emperor consented.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing that Kou Zhun might resent his having taken the chief ministership first, he asked that the Participants in Governance and the chief minister alternate days holding the seal and enter the Hall of Administration together; the Emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 時同列奏對多有異議，惟端罕所建明。

translations.literal: At the time colleagues memorializing in audience often had divergent opinions; only Duan rarely offered proposals.
translations.idiomatic: His colleagues often disagreed when memorializing in audience, but Lu Duan seldom advanced proposals of his own.

sentences.zh: 一日，內出手札戒諭：「自今中書事必經呂端詳酌，乃得聞奏。」

translations.literal: One day the palace issued a handwritten note of admonition: "From now on Secretariat affairs must pass through Lü Duan's careful consideration before they may be reported to the throne."
translations.idiomatic: One day the palace issued a handwritten directive: "Henceforth no Secretariat business may reach the throne until Lu Duan has reviewed it in detail."

sentences.zh: 端愈謙讓不自當。

translations.literal: Duan became all the more modest and declined to deem himself adequate.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Duan became only more modest and insisted he was unworthy of such trust.

sentences.zh: 初，李繼遷擾西鄙，保安軍奏獲其母。

translations.literal: Initially, Li Jiqian had harassed the western borders; Bao'an Army memorialized that his mother had been captured.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Li Jiqian had raided the western frontier; Bao'an Army reported that his mother had been taken captive.

sentences.zh: 至是，太宗欲誅之，以寇準居樞密副使，獨召與謀。

translations.literal: By this time the Emperor wished to execute her; because Kou Zhun held the post of Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, he summoned Kou alone to consult.
translations.idiomatic: Now the Emperor wished to put her to death. Because Kou Zhun was Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, he summoned him alone to deliberate.

sentences.zh: 準退，過相幕，端疑謀大事，邀謂準曰：「上戒君勿言於端乎？」

translations.literal: When Kou withdrew he passed the chief minister's quarters; Duan suspected a major matter was afoot and, intercepting him, said to Kou: "Did His Majesty warn you not to speak of this to Duan?"
translations.idiomatic: As Kou Zhun withdrew he passed the chief minister's quarters. Lu Duan suspected some weighty matter was afoot and stopped him: "Did His Majesty tell you not to speak of this to me?"

sentences.zh: 準曰：「否。」

translations.literal: Kou said: "No."
translations.idiomatic: Kou Zhun said, "No."

sentences.zh: 端曰：「邊鄙常事，端不必與知，若軍國大計，端備位宰相，不可不知也。」

translations.literal: Duan said: "Routine border affairs need not involve Duan; but if it is a great military or state design, Duan holds the chief minister's seat and cannot be kept ignorant."
translations.idiomatic: Lu Duan said, "Routine border affairs need not concern me, but if this is a matter of military or state policy, I hold the chief ministership and cannot be kept in the dark."

sentences.zh: 準遂告其故，端曰：「何以處之？」

translations.literal: Kou then told him the reason; Duan said: "How do you propose to handle it?"
translations.idiomatic: Kou Zhun then told him the whole story. Lu Duan asked, "What do you propose to do?"

sentences.zh: 準曰：「欲斬於保安軍北門外，以戒凶逆。」

translations.literal: Kou said: "I wish to behead her outside the north gate of Bao'an Army as a warning to the rebellious."
translations.idiomatic: Kou Zhun said, "I intend to execute her outside the north gate of Bao'an Army as a warning to the rebels."

sentences.zh: 端曰：「必若此，非計之得也，願少緩之，端將覆奏。」

translations.literal: Duan said: "If it must be done this way, the plan is not sound; please delay a little — Duan will memorialize again."
translations.idiomatic: Lu Duan said, "If that is your plan, it is not sound. Please hold off a little — I will memorialize the throne again."

sentences.zh: 入曰：「昔項羽得太公，欲烹之，高祖曰：『願分我一杯羹。』

translations.literal: Entering, he said: "Formerly Xiang Yu seized Lord Tai and wished to boil him; Emperor Gao said, 'I wish you would share with me a bowl of the broth.'
translations.idiomatic: Entering audience, he said, "When Xiang Yu seized the Grand Duke and threatened to boil him, Emperor Gao replied, 'I would like a bowl of that broth as well.'

sentences.zh: 夫舉大事不顧其親，況繼遷悖逆之人乎？

translations.literal: One who undertakes great affairs does not regard his kin — how much less a man rebellious and perverse like Jiqian?
translations.idiomatic: A man who undertakes great affairs does not spare even his kin — how much less a rebel and traitor like Li Jiqian?

sentences.zh: 陛下今日殺之，明日繼遷可擒乎？

translations.literal: If Your Majesty executes her today, can Jiqian be captured tomorrow?
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty executes her today, will Li Jiqian be captured tomorrow?

sentences.zh: 若其不然，徒結怨仇，愈堅其叛心爾。」

translations.literal: If not, you will only forge a bitter enmity and strengthen his rebellious heart all the more."
translations.idiomatic: If not, you will only deepen his hatred and harden his resolve to rebel."

sentences.zh: 太宗曰：「然則何如？」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Then what should be done?"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor asked, "Then what should we do?"

sentences.zh: 端曰：「以臣之愚，宜置於延州，使善養視之，以招來繼遷。

translations.literal: Duan said: "In this subject's humble view, she should be placed at Yan Prefecture and kindly cared for, to entice Jiqian to come in.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Duan said, "In my humble view, she should be kept at Yan Prefecture and treated well, to entice Li Jiqian to submit.

sentences.zh: 雖不能即降，終可以繫其心，而母死生之命在我矣。」

translations.literal: Though he may not surrender at once, in the end it will bind his heart — and his mother's life and death will lie in our hands."
translations.idiomatic: He may not surrender at once, but in time this will win his heart — and his mother's life or death will rest in our hands."

sentences.zh: 太宗撫髀稱善曰：「微卿，幾誤我事。」

translations.literal: The Emperor slapped his thigh in praise: "Were it not for you, I would almost have blundered in this affair."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor slapped his thigh in approval: "Without you, I would nearly have ruined this affair."

sentences.zh: 即用其策。

translations.literal: He immediately adopted the plan.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately adopted the plan.

sentences.zh: 其母後病死延州，繼遷尋亦死，繼遷子竟納款請命，端之力也。

translations.literal: The mother later died of illness at Yan; Jiqian soon died as well, and Jiqian's son in the end submitted and begged for orders — this was Duan's doing.
translations.idiomatic: His mother later died of illness at Yan; Li Jiqian soon died as well, and Jiqian's son eventually submitted and sought imperial orders — this was Lu Duan's achievement.

sentences.zh: 進門下侍郎兼兵部尚書。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Vice Director of the Secretariat and concurrently Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Vice Director of the Secretariat and concurrently Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 太宗不豫，真宗為皇太子，端日與太子問起居。

translations.literal: When Emperor Taizong fell ill, Zhenzong was crown prince; Duan daily went with the prince to inquire after his health.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taizong fell ill, Zhenzong was crown prince; Lu Duan went daily with the prince to inquire after the Emperor's health.

sentences.zh: 及疾大漸，內侍王繼恩忌太子英明，陰與參知政事李昌齡、殿前都指揮使李繼勳、知制誥胡旦謀立故楚王元佐。

translations.literal: When the illness grew grave, the inner attendant Wang Jien resented the prince's brilliance and secretly joined with Participant in Governance Li Changling, Commander of the Palace Front Li Jixun, and Drafting Academician Hu Dan to plot raising the former Prince of Chu Yuanzuo.
translations.idiomatic: As the illness worsened, the eunuch Wang Jien, resenting the crown prince's brilliance, secretly conspired with Li Changling, Participant in Governance, Li Jixun, Commander of the Palace Front, and Hu Dan, Drafting Academician, to install the former Prince of Chu Zhao Yuanzuo.

sentences.zh: 太宗崩，李皇后命繼恩召端，端知有變，鎖繼恩於閣內，使人守之而入。

translations.literal: When Taizong died, Empress Li ordered Jien to summon Duan; Duan knew something was amiss, locked Jien in a side room, set men to guard him, and entered.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong died, Empress Li ordered Wang Jien to summon Lu Duan. Sensing trouble, Duan locked Jien in a side chamber, posted guards, and entered the palace.

sentences.zh: 皇后曰：「宮車已晏駕，立嗣以長，順也，今將如何？」

translations.literal: The Empress said: "The imperial carriage has already traveled its evening course; to establish an heir by seniority is the proper way — what shall we do now?"
translations.idiomatic: The Empress said, "The imperial carriage has already departed on its final journey. To establish an heir by seniority is the proper course — what shall we do now?"

sentences.zh: 端曰：「先帝立太子正為今日，今始棄天下，豈可遽違命有異議邪？」

translations.literal: Duan said: "The late emperor established the crown prince precisely for this day; now that he has just left the realm, how could we suddenly disobey his command and raise other views?"
translations.idiomatic: Lu Duan said, "The late emperor named the crown prince precisely for this day. Now that he has just left the realm, how can we suddenly defy his command and entertain other candidates?"

sentences.zh: 乃奉太子至福寧庭中。

translations.literal: Thereupon he escorted the prince to the courtyard of Funing.
translations.idiomatic: He then escorted the crown prince to the courtyard of Funing.

sentences.zh: 真宗既立，垂簾引見群臣，端平立殿下不拜，請卷簾，升殿審視，然後降階，率群臣拜呼萬歲。

translations.literal: Once Zhenzong was enthroned, behind the curtain he received the officials; Duan stood level on the hall below without bowing, requested that the curtain be raised, ascended to the dais to scrutinize closely, then descended the steps, led the officials in bowing and shouting "Long live ten thousand years!"
translations.idiomatic: Once Zhenzong was enthroned, the officials were received behind a curtain. Lu Duan stood straight on the hall floor without bowing, asked that the curtain be raised, ascended to scrutinize the new emperor closely, then descended and led the officials in bowing and shouting "Long live ten thousand years!"

sentences.zh: 以繼勳為使相，赴陳州。

translations.literal: Li Jixun was made a commissioner on assignment, sent to Chen Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jixun was made a commissioner on assignment and sent to Chen Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 貶昌齡忠武軍司馬，繼恩右監門衛將軍、均州安置，旦除名流潯州，籍其家貲。

translations.literal: Li Changling was demoted to military aide of Zhongwu Army; Jien to Right General of the Jianmen Guard and settled at Jun Prefecture; Hu Dan was dismissed from office and banished to Xun Prefecture, and their household property was confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: Li Changling was demoted to military aide of Zhongwu Army; Wang Jien was made Right General of the Jianmen Guard and settled at Jun Prefecture; Hu Dan was dismissed and banished to Xun Prefecture, and their household property was confiscated.

sentences.zh: 真宗每見輔臣入對，惟於端肅然拱揖，不以名呼。

translations.literal: Whenever Zhenzong saw chief ministers enter for audience, toward Duan alone he would gravely press his hands in salute and not call him by name.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Zhenzong received his chief ministers in audience, toward Lu Duan alone he would gravely press his hands in salute and never call him by name.

sentences.zh: 又以端軀體洪大，宮庭階戺稍峻，特令梓人為納陛。

translations.literal: Also because Duan's stature was imposing and the palace steps somewhat steep, he specially ordered carpenters to make him mounting blocks.
translations.idiomatic: Because Lu Duan's frame was imposing and the palace steps rather steep, the Emperor specially ordered carpenters to make him mounting blocks.

sentences.zh: 嘗召對便殿，訪軍國大事經久之制，端陳當世急務，皆有條理，真宗嘉納。

translations.literal: Once summoned to the Hall of Convenience, the Emperor inquired into longstanding systems of military and state affairs; Duan laid out urgent tasks of the age, all with proper order, and Zhenzong commended and accepted them.
translations.idiomatic: Once summoned to the Hall of Convenience, the Emperor asked about longstanding institutions of military and state policy. Lu Duan set forth the urgent affairs of the day in well-ordered fashion, and Zhenzong commended and accepted his counsel.

sentences.zh: 加右僕射，監修國史。

translations.literal: He was given the additional title Right Vice Director and Supervisor of the National History.
translations.idiomatic: He was given the additional titles Right Vice Director and Supervisor of the National History.

sentences.zh: 明年夏，被疾，詔免常參，就中書視事。

translations.literal: The next summer he fell ill; an edict excused him from regular attendance and allowed him to conduct business at the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: The following summer he fell ill. An edict excused him from regular court attendance and allowed him to conduct Secretariat business from home.

sentences.zh: 上疏求解，不許。

translations.literal: He memorialized requesting release; this was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized requesting release from office, but the request was denied.

sentences.zh: 十月，以太子太保罷。

translations.literal: In the tenth month he was dismissed as Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he was dismissed with the title Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 在告三百日，有司言當罷奉，詔賜如故。

translations.literal: During three hundred days of sick leave, the relevant office said his stipend should cease; an edict ordered that it be granted as before.
translations.idiomatic: After three hundred days on sick leave, the relevant office ruled that his stipend should cease, but an edict ordered that it continue as before.

sentences.zh: 車駕臨問，端不能興，撫慰甚至。

translations.literal: The imperial carriage came in person to inquire; Duan could not rise, and the consolation extended to the utmost.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor came in person to inquire after him. Lu Duan could not rise, and the imperial consolation was profuse.

sentences.zh: 卒，年六十六，贈司空，諡正惠，追封妻李氏涇國夫人，以其子藩為太子中舍，荀大理評事，蔚千牛備身，藹殿中省進馬。

translations.literal: He died at sixty-six; posthumously enfeoffed as Minister of Works, posthumous title Zhenghui; his wife Lady Li was enfeoffed Lady of Jing; his sons Fan as Household Attendant of the Heir Apparent, Xun as Assessor of the Court of Judicial Review, Wei as Guardsman of the Heir Apparent's thousand riders, and Ai as Handler of Tribute Horses in the Palace Service.
translations.idiomatic: He died at sixty-six. He was posthumously enfeoffed as Minister of Works with the posthumous title Zhenghui. His wife Lady Li was enfeoffed Lady of Jing. His sons Fan, Xun, Wei, and Ai were appointed Household Attendant of the Heir Apparent, Assessor of the Court of Judicial Review, Guardsman of the Heir Apparent's thousand riders, and Handler of Tribute Horses in the Palace Service, respectively.

sentences.zh: 端姿儀瑰秀，有器量，寬厚多恕，善談謔，意豁如也。

translations.literal: Duan's bearing was splendid and he had capacity; he was generous and forgiving, skilled in wit and banter, his mind broad and easy.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Duan's bearing was splendid and he possessed great capacity. He was generous and forgiving, skilled in wit and banter, and his mind was broad and at ease.

sentences.zh: 雖屢經擯退，未嘗以得喪介懷。

translations.literal: Though repeatedly demoted and dismissed, he never let gain or loss weigh on his heart.
translations.idiomatic: Though repeatedly demoted and dismissed, he never let gain or loss trouble his heart.

sentences.zh: 善與人交，輕財好施，未嘗問家事。

translations.literal: He was good at friendship, light with wealth and fond of giving, and never inquired into household affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He made friends easily, was free with wealth and fond of giving, and never troubled himself with household affairs.

sentences.zh: 李惟清自知樞密改御史中丞，意端抑己，及端免朝謁，乃彈奏常參官疾告逾年受奉者，又構人訟堂吏過失，欲以中端。

translations.literal: Li Weiqing, knowing himself demoted from the Bureau of Military Affairs to Censor in Chief, thought Duan had restrained him; when Duan was excused from court audience he impeached regular officials who on sick leave over a year still received salaries, and also got someone to sue the hall clerks for faults, intending to strike at Duan.
translations.idiomatic: Li Weiqing, demoted from the Bureau of Military Affairs to Censor in Chief, believed Lu Duan had held him back. When Duan was excused from court attendance, Weiqing impeached regular officials who had received salaries for more than a year on sick leave, and also arranged lawsuits against the hall clerks for misconduct, intending to strike at Duan.

sentences.zh: 端曰：「吾直道而行，無所愧畏，風波之言不足慮也。」

translations.literal: Duan said: "I walk the straight path and have nothing to fear; talk of storms is not worth worrying about."
translations.idiomatic: Lu Duan said, "I walk the straight path and have nothing to fear. Talk of storms is not worth worrying about."

sentences.zh: 端祖兗，嘗事滄州節度劉守文為判官。

translations.literal: Duan's grandfather Yan had once served Liu Shouwen, military commissioner of Cang Prefecture, as judge.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Duan's grandfather Yan had once served Liu Shouwen, military commissioner of Cang Prefecture, as administrative aide.

sentences.zh: 守文之亂，兗舉族被害。

translations.literal: In Shouwen's rebellion, Yan's entire clan was killed.
translations.idiomatic: During Shouwen's rebellion, Yan's entire clan was slaughtered.

sentences.zh: 時父琦方幼，同郡趙玉冒鋒刃紿監者曰：「此予之弟，非呂氏子也。」

translations.literal: At the time his father Qi was still young; Zhao Yu of the same commandery braved blade's edge and deceived the guard, saying: "This is my younger brother — not a son of the Lü clan."
translations.idiomatic: His father Qi was still a child. Zhao Yu of the same commandery braved the blades and deceived the guard, saying, "This is my younger brother — not a son of the Lü clan."

sentences.zh: 遂得免。

translations.literal: Thus he escaped death.
translations.idiomatic: Thus Qi escaped death.

sentences.zh: 玉子文度為耀帥，文度孫紹宗十餘歲，端視如己子，表薦賜出身。

translations.literal: Yu's son Wendu became military commissioner of Yao; Wendu's grandson Shaozong was barely over ten — Duan regarded him as his own son, memorialized recommending him, and granted him initial court rank.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Yu's son Wendu became military commissioner of Yao. When Wendu's grandson Shaozong was barely ten, Lu Duan treated him as his own son, memorialized recommending him, and secured him initial court rank.

sentences.zh: 故相馮道，鄉里世舊，道子正之病廢，端分奉給之。

translations.literal: Former chief minister Feng Dao was a hereditary acquaintance in their home district; Dao's son Zheng was ill and disabled — Duan shared his stipend to support him.
translations.idiomatic: Former chief minister Feng Dao was a family friend from their home district. When Dao's son Zheng fell ill and was disabled, Lu Duan shared his stipend to support him.

sentences.zh: 端兩使絕域，其國歎重之，後有使往者，每問端為宰相否，其名顯如此。

translations.literal: Duan twice went as envoy to distant regions; those countries admired and esteemed him, and later when envoys came they always asked whether Duan was still chief minister — his fame was so renowned.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Duan twice served as envoy to distant lands, where his hosts admired him greatly. Later envoys from those countries always asked whether Lu Duan was still chief minister — such was his renown.

sentences.zh: 景德二年，真宗聞端後嗣不振，又錄蔚為奉禮郎。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jingde, Zhenzong heard that Duan's later descendants were not prospering and again recorded Wei as Master of Ceremonials.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jingde, Zhenzong heard that Lu Duan's descendants were faring poorly and again appointed Wei as Master of Ceremonials.

sentences.zh: 藩後病足，不任朝謁，請告累年，有司奏罷其奉，真宗特令復舊官，分司西京，給奉家居養病。

translations.literal: Fan later suffered crippled feet and could not attend court; he requested sick leave for many years; the relevant office memorialized to cut his salary; Zhenzong specially ordered restoration of his former post, assigned to the Western Capital branch office, with stipend to live at home and nurse his illness.
translations.idiomatic: Fan later suffered crippled feet and could not attend court. After years of sick leave, the relevant office memorialized to cut his salary, but Zhenzong specially restored his former post, assigned him to the Western Capital branch office, and granted a stipend to live at home and nurse his illness.

sentences.zh: 端不蓄貲產，藩兄弟貧匱，又迫婚嫁，因質其居第。

translations.literal: Duan accumulated no property; Fan and his brothers were destitute and pressed by marriage obligations, and therefore mortgaged the family residence.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Duan had accumulated no property. Fan and his brothers were destitute and pressed by marriage expenses, and therefore mortgaged the family residence.

sentences.zh: 真宗時，出內府錢五百萬贖還之。

translations.literal: In Zhenzong's time, five million coins from the inner treasury were issued to redeem it.
translations.idiomatic: During Zhenzong's reign, five million coins from the inner treasury were issued to redeem it.

sentences.zh: 又別賜金帛，俾償宿負，遣使檢校家事。

translations.literal: Gold and silk were also separately bestowed to pay old debts, and envoys were sent to inspect household affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Gold and silk were also bestowed separately to pay off old debts, and envoys were sent to inspect the family's affairs.

sentences.zh: 藩、荀皆至國子博士，蔚至太子中舍。

translations.literal: Fan and Xun both reached Doctor of the National University; Wei reached Household Attendant of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Fan and Xun both rose to Doctor of the National University; Wei reached Household Attendant of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 畢士安

translations.literal: Bi Shi'an
translations.idiomatic: Bi Shi'an

sentences.zh: 畢士安，字仁叟，代州雲中人。

translations.literal: Bi Shi'an, styled Rensou, was a native of Yunzhong in Dai Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Bi Shi'an, styled Rensou, was a native of Yunzhong in Dai Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 曾祖宗昱，本縣令。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Zongyu was magistrate of the home county.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Zongyu served as magistrate of his home county.

sentences.zh: 祖球，本州別駕。

translations.literal: His grandfather Qiu was Vice Governor of the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Qiu served as Vice Governor of the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父乂林，累辟使府，終觀城令，因家焉。

translations.literal: His father Yilin was repeatedly summoned to commissioner staffs and finally served as magistrate of Guancheng, whereupon the family settled there.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yilin was repeatedly summoned to commissioner staffs and finally served as magistrate of Guancheng, where the family then settled.

sentences.zh: 士安少好學，事繼母祝氏以孝聞。

translations.literal: Shi'an from youth loved learning and served his stepmother Lady Zhu with such filial piety that it was renowned.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Shi'an loved learning and served his stepmother Lady Zhu with such filial devotion that his reputation spread.

sentences.zh: 祝氏曰：「學必求良師友。」

translations.literal: Lady Zhu said: "In study one must seek good teachers and friends."
translations.idiomatic: Lady Zhu said, "In study one must seek worthy teachers and companions."

sentences.zh: 乃與如宋，又如鄭，得楊璞、韓丕、劉錫為友，因為鄭人。

translations.literal: Thereupon he traveled with her to Song and again to Zheng, befriending Yang Pu, Han Pi, and Liu Xi, and thus became a man of Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: He then traveled with her to the Song capital and on to Zheng, where he befriended Yang Pu, Han Pi, and Liu Xi, and thus became a man of Zheng.

sentences.zh: 乾德四年，舉進士。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Qiande he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Qiande he passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 邠帥楊廷璋辟幕府，掌書奏。

translations.literal: Military Commissioner of Bin Yang Tingzhang recruited him to his staff to manage documents and memorials.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Tingzhang, military commissioner of Bin, recruited him to his staff to manage documents and memorials.

sentences.zh: 開寶四年，歷濟州團練推官，專掌筦榷，歲課增羡。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Kaibao he served as recorder on the military staff of Ji Prefecture, solely in charge of monopoly transport; annual revenue increased.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Kaibao he served as recorder on the military staff of Ji Prefecture, solely in charge of monopoly revenues, and annual receipts increased substantially.

sentences.zh: 改兗州觀察推官。

translations.literal: He was transferred to recorder on the observation staff of Yan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to recorder on the observation staff of Yan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 太平興國初，為大理寺丞，領三門發運事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taiping Xingguo he was made Vice Director of the Court of Judicial Review and supervised the Three Gates transport office.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Taiping Xingguo he was appointed Vice Director of the Court of Judicial Review and placed in charge of the Three Gates transport office.

sentences.zh: 吳越錢俶納土，選知台州，言：「錢氏上圖籍，有司皆張侈賦數，今湖海新民始得天子命吏，宜有安輯，願一用舊籍。」

translations.literal: When Qian Chu of Wuyue submitted his territory, [Shi'an] was chosen to know Taizhou and said: "The Qian house has presented maps and registers; the offices have all inflated tax quotas. Now the people of lakes and sea are newly obtaining the Son of Heaven's appointed officials — there ought to be reassurance and settlement; I wish to use the old registers throughout."
translations.idiomatic: When Qian Chu of Wuyue submitted his territory, Shi'an was chosen prefect of Taizhou and said, "The Qian house has presented its maps and registers, but the offices have inflated the tax quotas. The people of the coastal regions are only now receiving the Son of Heaven's appointed officials and need reassurance. I ask that the old registers be used throughout."

sentences.zh: 詔從之。

translations.literal: An edict followed this.
translations.idiomatic: An edict approved his request.

sentences.zh: 明年，遷左贊善大夫，徙饒州，改殿中丞。

translations.literal: The next year he was promoted to Left Supporter of Virtue, transferred to Rao Prefecture, and made Palace Director.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was promoted to Left Supporter of Virtue, transferred to Rao Prefecture, and appointed Palace Director.

sentences.zh: 召還，為監察御史。

translations.literal: He was recalled and made Supervising Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to court and appointed Supervising Censor.

sentences.zh: 復出知乾州，以母老願降任就養，改監汝州稻田務。

translations.literal: He went out again to know Qian Prefecture; because his mother was old he wished to accept a lower post to stay near and support her, and was changed to superintendent of the paddy-field office in Ru Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out again as prefect of Qian, but with his mother aging he asked for a lower appointment so he could care for her nearby and was made superintendent of the paddy-field office in Ru Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 雍熙二年，諸王出閤，慎擇僚屬。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongxi the princes left the inner quarters; staff members were carefully chosen.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yongxi the princes were formally established in their households, and staff members were chosen with care.

sentences.zh: 以虞部郎中王龜從兼陳王府記室參軍，水部員外郎王素兼韓王府記室參軍，秘書丞張茂直兼益王府記室參軍，士安遷左拾遺兼冀王府記室參軍。

translations.literal: Wang Guicong, Director of the Bureau of Parks and Forests, was additionally made Recorder of the Prince of Chen's household; Wang Su, Vice Director of the Bureau of Works, was additionally made Recorder of the Prince of Han's household; Zhang Maozhi, Secretary of the Secretariat, was additionally made Recorder of the Prince of Yi's household; Shi'an was promoted to Left Remonstrance Censor and additionally made Recorder of the Prince of Ji's household.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Guicong, Director of the Bureau of Parks and Forests, was also appointed recorder for the Prince of Chen; Wang Su, Vice Director of the Bureau of Works, for the Prince of Han; Zhang Maozhi, Secretary of the Secretariat, for the Prince of Yi; and Shi'an was promoted to Left Remonstrance Censor and also made recorder for the Prince of Ji.

sentences.zh: 太宗召謂曰：「諸子生長宮庭，未閒外事，年漸成人，必資良士贊導，使日聞忠孝之道，卿等勉之。」

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong summoned them and said: "My sons have grown up in the palace and are unacquainted with affairs outside; as they gradually become adults, they must rely on good gentlemen to assist and guide them, so that day by day they hear the way of loyalty and filial piety — do your utmost."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong summoned them and said, "My sons have grown up in the palace and know nothing of the world outside. As they come of age, they will need worthy men to guide them and teach them loyalty and filial piety every day. Do your utmost."

sentences.zh: 賜襲衣、銀帶、鞍勒馬。

translations.literal: He granted them ceremonial robes, silver belts, saddles, bridles, and horses.
translations.idiomatic: He also granted them ceremonial robes, silver belts, saddles, bridles, and horses.

sentences.zh: 士安本名士元，以「元」犯王諱，遂改焉。

translations.literal: Shi'an's original name was Shiyuan; because "yuan" violated a prince's taboo, he changed it accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: Shi'an had originally been named Shiyuan, but changed it because the character "yuan" was taboo for one of the princes.

sentences.zh: 遷考功員外郎。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Vice Director of the Bureau of Merit.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Vice Director of the Bureau of Merit.

sentences.zh: 端拱中，詔王府僚屬各獻所著文，太宗閱視累日，問近臣曰：「其才已見矣，其行孰優？」

translations.literal: During the Duanhe era, an edict ordered the staff of the princely households each to submit writings they had composed. Emperor Taizong reviewed them for many days and asked his close ministers: "Their talent is already apparent — whose conduct is superior?"
translations.idiomatic: During the Duanhe era, an edict required each member of the princes' staffs to submit his writings. Emperor Taizong read them for days and asked his close ministers, "I can see their talent — but whose character is best?"

sentences.zh: 或以士安對。

translations.literal: Someone answered with Shi'an.
translations.idiomatic: Someone replied that Shi'an was.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「正協朕意。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "This precisely accords with my intention."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "That is exactly what I think."

sentences.zh: 俄以本官知制誥，王請對願留府邸，不許。

translations.literal: Soon, while retaining his original rank, he was made Drafting Edict Officer; the Prince requested audience wishing to keep him at the princely residence, but this was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, while retaining his original rank, he was made Drafting Edict Officer. The Prince asked to keep him at the princely residence, but the request was denied.

sentences.zh: 淳化二年，召入翰林為學士。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chunhua he was summoned into the Hanlin Academy as Academician.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Chunhua he was summoned to the Hanlin Academy as an Academician.

sentences.zh: 大臣以張洎薦，太宗曰：「洎視畢士安詞藝踐歷固不減，但履行遠在下爾。」

translations.literal: Grandees recommended him through Zhang Zhi; Emperor Taizong said: "Compared with Bi Shi'an, Zhi is certainly not inferior in literary skill and official experience, but in conduct he falls far below."
translations.idiomatic: Grandees recommended him through Zhang Zhi. Emperor Taizong said, "Zhi is certainly no less accomplished than Bi Shi'an in literary skill and official experience, but in personal conduct he falls far short."

sentences.zh: 士安以父名乂林抗章引避，朝議謂二名不偏諱，不聽。

translations.literal: Shi'an submitted a memorial requesting withdrawal because his father's name was Yilin; court discussion held that the two-character taboo rule of avoiding neither character separately applied and did not approve.
translations.idiomatic: Bi Shi'an submitted a memorial asking to withdraw because his father's name was Yilin. Court discussion held that the rule against tabooing only one of two characters in a name did not apply, and the request was denied.

sentences.zh: 三年，與蘇易簡同知貢舉，加主客郎中。

translations.literal: In the third year he served with Su Yijian as co-director of the civil examinations and was additionally made Director of the Bureau of Receptions.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he served with Su Yijian as co-director of the civil examinations and was additionally appointed Director of the Bureau of Receptions.

sentences.zh: 以疾請外，改右諫議大夫、知潁州。

translations.literal: Requesting assignment outside the capital on account of illness, he was changed to Right Remonstrance Grandee and made prefect of Ying Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Citing illness, he requested a provincial appointment and was made Right Remonstrance Grandee and prefect of Ying Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 真宗以壽王尹開封府，召為判官。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhenzong, as Prince of Shou, was administering Kaifeng Prefecture, [Shi'an] was summoned as administrative judge.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhenzong, as Prince of Shou, was administering Kaifeng Prefecture, Shi'an was summoned to serve as administrative judge.

sentences.zh: 及為皇太子，以兼右庶子遷給事中。

translations.literal: When [Zhenzong] became heir apparent, [Shi'an] was promoted to Supervising Censor on account of his additional post as Right Companion.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhenzong became heir apparent, Shi'an was promoted to Supervising Censor while serving additionally as Right Companion.

sentences.zh: 登位，命權知開封府事，拜工部侍郎、樞密直學士。

translations.literal: Upon ascending the throne, [Zhenzong] ordered him to serve temporarily as prefect of Kaifeng, and appointed him Vice Minister of Works and Academician Directly Attached to the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhenzong ascended the throne, he ordered Shi'an to serve temporarily as prefect of Kaifeng and appointed him Vice Minister of Works and Academician Directly Attached to the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 時近臣有怙勢強取民間定婚女，其家訴於府，士安因對奏，還之。

translations.literal: At that time a close minister relying on his power forcibly took a betrothed daughter from among the people; her family appealed to the prefecture, and when Shi'an was at audience he memorialized and restored her.
translations.idiomatic: At that time a close minister used his influence to seize a betrothed commoner's daughter. When her family appealed to the prefecture, Shi'an memorialized at audience and had her returned.

sentences.zh: 宮府常從為廷職者，每授任於外，必令士安戒勖。

translations.literal: Whenever palace attendants who had become court officials were appointed to posts outside the capital, Shi'an was always ordered to admonish and instruct them.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever palace attendants who had become court officials were sent out on provincial appointments, Shi'an was always ordered to admonish and instruct them.

sentences.zh: 咸平初，辭府職，拜禮部侍郎，復為翰林學士。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xianping he resigned his prefectural post, was appointed Vice Minister of Rites, and again became Hanlin Academician.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Xianping he resigned his post at the prefecture, was appointed Vice Minister of Rites, and again became a Hanlin Academician.

sentences.zh: 詔選官校勘《三國志》、《晉》、《唐書》。

translations.literal: An edict ordered officials chosen to collate the Records of the Three Kingdoms, the Jin histories, and the Tang histories.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered officials selected to collate the Records of the Three Kingdoms, the Jin histories, and the Tang histories.

sentences.zh: 或有言兩晉事多鄙惡不可流行者。

translations.literal: Some said that matters of the two Jin dynasties were largely base and vile and should not be circulated.
translations.idiomatic: Some argued that the two Jin dynasties contained too many base and shameful episodes to be circulated.

sentences.zh: 真宗以語宰相，士安曰：「惡以戒世，善以勸後。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhenzong spoke of this to the chief minister; Shi'an said: "Evil serves to warn the age, and good serves to encourage posterity.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhenzong raised the matter with the chief minister. Shi'an said, "Evil warns the age, and good encourages posterity.

sentences.zh: 善惡之事，《春秋》備載。」

translations.literal: Matters of good and evil — the Spring and Autumn Annals records them fully."
translations.idiomatic: Good and evil alike — the Spring and Autumn Annals records them in full."

sentences.zh: 真宗然之，遂命刊刻。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhenzong agreed and ordered them printed.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhenzong agreed and ordered the texts printed.

sentences.zh: 士安以目疾求解，改兵部侍郎，出知潞州，特加月給之數。

translations.literal: Shi'an requested relief from office because of eye disease; he was changed to Vice Minister of War, sent out as prefect of Lu Prefecture, and his monthly stipend was specially increased.
translations.idiomatic: Shi'an asked to leave office because of eye disease. He was made Vice Minister of War and sent out as prefect of Lu Prefecture, with a special increase to his monthly stipend.

sentences.zh: 入為翰林侍讀學士。

translations.literal: He entered [court] as Hanlin Academician Reader-in-Waiting.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to court as Hanlin Academician Reader-in-Waiting.

sentences.zh: 景德初，兼秘書監。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jingde he additionally served as Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Jingde he additionally served as Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 契丹謀入境，士安首疏五事應詔，陳選將、餉兵、理財之策，真宗嘉納。

translations.literal: When the Khitan plotted to invade the borders, Shi'an was first to submit a five-point memorial in response to an edict, setting forth policies for selecting generals, provisioning troops, and managing finances; Emperor Zhenzong praised and adopted them.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan plotted to invade, Shi'an was the first to submit a five-point memorial in response to an edict, outlining policies for selecting generals, provisioning troops, and managing finances. Emperor Zhenzong praised and adopted his proposals.

sentences.zh: 李沆卒，進士安吏部侍郎、參知政事。

translations.literal: When Li Hang died, Shi'an was promoted to Vice Minister of Personnel and made Participant in Governance.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Hang died, Shi'an was promoted to Vice Minister of Personnel and appointed Participant in Governance.

sentences.zh: 入謝，真宗曰：「未也，行且相卿。」

translations.literal: When he entered to give thanks, Emperor Zhenzong said: "Not yet — presently I shall make you chief minister."
translations.idiomatic: When he came in to give thanks, Emperor Zhenzong said, "Not yet — soon I shall make you chief minister."

sentences.zh: 士安頓首。

translations.literal: Shi'an bowed his head to the ground.
translations.idiomatic: Shi'an kowtowed.

sentences.zh: 真宗曰：「朕倚卿以輔相，豈特今日。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhenzong said: "I rely on you as my assisting minister — and not only today.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhenzong said, "I rely on you as my chief minister — and not only today.

sentences.zh: 然時方多事，求與卿同進者，其誰可？」

translations.literal: Yet the times are beset with many affairs; whom can I advance together with you?"
translations.idiomatic: But these are troubled times. Whom can I promote to serve alongside you?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「宰相者，必有其器，乃可居其位，臣駑朽，實不足以勝任。

translations.literal: He replied: "A chief minister must have the capacity for it before he can occupy the post; I am worn and decayed and truly insufficient to bear the responsibility.
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "A chief minister must have the capacity for the office before he can hold it. I am worn out and truly unfit for the task.

sentences.zh: 寇準兼資忠義，善斷大事，此宰相才也。」

translations.literal: Kou Zhun combines loyalty and righteousness and is adept at deciding great affairs — this is talent for chief minister."
translations.idiomatic: Kou Zhun combines loyalty and righteousness and is adept at deciding great affairs — he has the makings of a chief minister."

sentences.zh: 真宗曰：「聞其好剛使氣。」

translations.literal: Emperor Zhenzong said: "I have heard that he loves to be unyielding and works his temper."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhenzong said, "I have heard that he is stubborn and quick to anger."

sentences.zh: 又對曰：「準方正慷慨有大節，忘身徇國，秉道疾邪，此其素所蓄積，朝臣罕出其右者，第不為流俗所喜。

translations.literal: He replied again: "Kou is upright, generous, and possessed of great integrity; he forgets himself and serves the state, upholds the Way and hates evil — this is what he has long accumulated. Among court ministers few surpass him, only he is not favored by vulgar fashion.
translations.idiomatic: He replied again, "Kou Zhun is upright, generous, and possessed of great integrity. He forgets himself in service to the state, upholds the Way, and hates evil — qualities he has long cultivated. Few court ministers surpass him, though he is not popular with the vulgar crowd.

sentences.zh: 今天下之民雖蒙休德，涵養安佚，而西北跳梁為邊境患，若準者正所宜用也。」

translations.literal: Today the people under Heaven, though enjoying repose and kindness, are nurtured in ease — yet in the northwest the unruly make trouble as a border scourge; a man like Kou Zhun is exactly what ought to be employed."
translations.idiomatic: The people may enjoy peace and kindness today, but in the northwest the unruly still plague the borders. A man like Kou Zhun is exactly what should be employed."

sentences.zh: 真宗曰：「然，當藉卿宿德鎮之。」

translations.literal: Emperor Zhenzong said: "So it is — I shall rely on your longstanding virtue to keep him in check."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhenzong said, "So be it — I shall rely on your longstanding virtue to keep him in check."

sentences.zh: 未閱月，以本官與準同拜平章事。

translations.literal: Within less than a month, retaining his original rank, he and Kou Zhun were together appointed Grand Counselors of State.
translations.idiomatic: Within less than a month, while retaining his original rank, he and Kou Zhun were together appointed Grand Counselors of State.

sentences.zh: 士安兼監修國史，居準上。

translations.literal: Shi'an additionally supervised compilation of the national history and ranked above Kou Zhun.
translations.idiomatic: Shi'an additionally supervised compilation of the national history and ranked above Kou Zhun.

sentences.zh: 準為相，守正嫉惡，小人日思所以傾之。

translations.literal: Kou Zhun as chief minister upheld integrity and hated evil; petty men daily thought of ways to overturn him.
translations.idiomatic: As chief minister, Kou Zhun upheld integrity and hated evil, and petty men daily schemed to bring him down.

sentences.zh: 有布衣申宗古告準交通安王元傑，準皇恐，莫知所自明。

translations.literal: A commoner named Shen Zonggu reported that Kou Zhun had improper dealings with Prince An Yuanjie; Kou Zhun was terrified and did not know how to clear himself.
translations.idiomatic: A commoner named Shen Zonggu accused Kou Zhun of secret dealings with Prince An Yuanjie. Kou Zhun was terrified and did not know how to clear himself.

sentences.zh: 士安力辯其誣，下宗古吏，具得姦罔，斬之，準乃安。

translations.literal: Shi'an forcefully argued that this was a false charge; Zonggu was handed over to the judicial officers, the fraud was fully established, and he was executed — only then did Kou Zhun feel secure.
translations.idiomatic: Shi'an forcefully argued that the charge was false. Zonggu was handed over to the judicial officers, the fraud was fully established, and he was executed — only then did Kou Zhun feel secure.

sentences.zh: 景德元年九月，契丹統軍撻覽引兵分掠威虜、順安、北平，侵保州，攻定武，數為諸軍所卻，益東駐陽城澱，遂攻高陽，不得逞，轉窺貝、冀、天雄，兵號二十萬。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the first year of Jingde, the Khitan commander-in-chief Tayan led troops to plunder separately at Weilu, Shun'an, and Beiping, invaded Ba Prefecture, attacked Dingwu, was repeatedly repelled by various armies, moved further east to camp at Yangcheng Marsh, then attacked Gaoyang without success, turned to cast eyes on Bei, Ji, and Tianxiong — his forces numbered two hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the first year of Jingde, the Khitan commander-in-chief Tayan led troops to raid Weilu, Shun'an, and Beiping, invaded Ba Prefecture, and attacked Dingwu. He was repeatedly repelled by Song forces, moved east to camp at Yangcheng Marsh, then attacked Gaoyang without success and turned toward Bei, Ji, and Tianxiong. His army was said to number two hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 真宗坐便殿，問策安出。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhenzong sat in the informal hall and asked where strategy should come from.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhenzong sat in the informal hall and asked where strategy should come from.

sentences.zh: 士安與寇準條所以禦備狀，又合議請真宗幸澶淵。

translations.literal: Shi'an and Kou Zhun laid out in detail the measures for defense and together proposed that Emperor Zhenzong proceed to Chanyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Shi'an and Kou Zhun laid out the defensive measures in detail and together proposed that Emperor Zhenzong proceed to Chanyuan.

sentences.zh: 士安言澶淵之行，當在仲冬；

translations.literal: Shi'an said the journey to Chanyuan ought to take place in midwinter;
translations.idiomatic: Shi'an said the journey to Chanyuan ought to wait until midwinter;

sentences.zh: 準謂當亟往，不可緩。

translations.literal: Kou Zhun said they should go at once and must not delay.
translations.idiomatic: Kou Zhun said they should go at once and must not delay.

sentences.zh: 卒用士安議。

translations.literal: In the end Shi'an's proposal was adopted.
translations.idiomatic: In the end Shi'an's proposal was adopted.

sentences.zh: 初，咸平六年，雲州觀察使王繼忠戰陷契丹。

translations.literal: Previously, in the sixth year of Xianping, Wang Jizhong, Observation Commissioner of Yun Prefecture, was captured in battle by the Khitan.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, in the sixth year of Xianping, Wang Jizhong, Observation Commissioner of Yun Prefecture, had been captured in battle by the Khitan.

sentences.zh: 至是，為契丹奏請議和。

translations.literal: At this time he presented a memorial on the Khitan's behalf requesting peace negotiations.
translations.idiomatic: Now he presented a memorial on the Khitan's behalf requesting peace negotiations.

sentences.zh: 大臣莫敢如何，獨士安以為可信，力贊真宗當羈縻不絕，漸許其成。

translations.literal: Grandees none dared say what to do; only Shi'an deemed it credible and strongly urged Emperor Zhenzong to keep ties through gentle restraint without breaking off, gradually permitting it to succeed.
translations.idiomatic: None of the grandees dared say what to do. Only Shi'an deemed the overture credible and strongly urged Emperor Zhenzong to keep diplomatic ties open and gradually allow peace to succeed.

sentences.zh: 真宗謂敵悍如此，恐不可保。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhenzong said the enemy was so fierce that he feared peace could not be maintained.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhenzong said the enemy was so fierce that he feared peace could not be maintained.

sentences.zh: 士安曰：「臣嘗得契丹降人，言其雖深入，屢挫不甚得志，陰欲引去而恥無名，且彼寧不畏人乘虛覆其巢穴，此請殆不妄。

translations.literal: Shi'an said: "Your subject once obtained a Khitan defector who said that though they had penetrated deeply, they had suffered repeated setbacks and were not greatly achieving their aims; secretly they wished to withdraw but were shamed at doing so without a pretext. Moreover, would they not fear that someone might exploit the opening to overrun their nest? This request is probably not false.
translations.idiomatic: Shi'an said, "I once obtained a Khitan defector who said that although they had penetrated deeply, they had suffered repeated setbacks and were not achieving their aims. Secretly they wished to withdraw but were ashamed to do so without a pretext. Moreover, would they not fear that we might exploit the opening to overrun their homeland? This request is probably genuine.

sentences.zh: 繼忠之奏，臣請任之。」

translations.literal: As for Jizhong's memorial, your subject asks to take responsibility for it."
translations.idiomatic: As for Jizhong's memorial, I ask to take responsibility for it."

sentences.zh: 真宗喜，手詔繼忠，許其請和。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhenzong was pleased, personally drafted an edict to Jizhong, and granted the request for peace.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhenzong was pleased, personally drafted an edict to Jizhong, and granted the request for peace.

sentences.zh: 時已詔巡幸，而議者猶哄哄，二三大臣有進金陵及成都圖者。

translations.literal: At that time an edict for the imperial progress had already been issued, yet those who deliberated still clamored; two or three grandees even submitted maps of Jinling and Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: An edict for the imperial progress had already been issued, yet the deliberators still clamored. Two or three grandees even submitted maps of Jinling and Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 士安亟同準請對，力陳其不可，惟堅定前計。

translations.literal: Shi'an quickly joined Kou Zhun in requesting audience, forcefully stated that this could not be done, and held firm to the earlier plan.
translations.idiomatic: Shi'an quickly joined Kou Zhun in requesting audience, forcefully argued that retreat was impossible, and held firm to the earlier plan.

sentences.zh: 真宗嚴兵將行，太白晝見，流星出上臺北貫斗魁。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhenzong reviewed troops and was about to depart when Venus appeared in daylight and a shooting star emerged north of Upper Terrace and pierced through the Dipper's ladle.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhenzong reviewed troops and was about to depart when Venus appeared in daylight and a shooting star emerged north of Upper Terrace and pierced through the Dipper's ladle.

sentences.zh: 或言兵未宜北，或言大臣應之。

translations.literal: Some said troops ought not go north; others said a grand minister would answer the omen.
translations.idiomatic: Some said troops ought not go north; others said a grand minister would answer the omen.

sentences.zh: 士安適臥疾，移書準曰：「屢請舁疾從行，手詔不許，今大計已定，唯君勉之。

translations.literal: Shi'an happened to be ill in bed and sent a letter to Kou Zhun: "I have repeatedly asked to be carried despite illness to follow on the journey, but the personal edict did not permit it. Now the great plan is settled — only you must do your utmost.
translations.idiomatic: Shi'an happened to be ill in bed and sent a letter to Kou Zhun: "I have repeatedly asked to be carried despite illness to follow on the journey, but the personal edict did not permit it. Now the great plan is settled — only you must do your utmost.

sentences.zh: 士安得以身當星變而就國事，心所願也。」

translations.literal: That Shi'an might take the celestial anomaly upon himself and thereby fulfill affairs of state is what my heart desires."
translations.idiomatic: If I could take the celestial anomaly upon myself and thereby serve the state, that would be my heart's desire."

sentences.zh: 已而少間，追至澶淵，見於行在。

translations.literal: After a brief recovery he hurried after them to Chanyuan and was received at the imperial headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: After a brief recovery he hurried after them to Chanyuan and was received at the imperial headquarters.

sentences.zh: 時已聚兵數十萬，契丹大震，猶乘眾掠德清。

translations.literal: By then several hundred thousand troops had been assembled; the Khitan were greatly shaken, yet still trusting their numbers they plundered Deqing.
translations.idiomatic: By then several hundred thousand troops had been assembled. The Khitan were greatly shaken, yet still trusting their numbers they plundered Deqing.

sentences.zh: 至澶北鄙，為伏弩發射，撻覽死，眾潰遁去。

translations.literal: When they reached the northern marches of Chanyuan, hidden crossbows fired; Tayan died, and the host broke up and fled.
translations.idiomatic: When they reached the northern marches of Chanyuan, hidden crossbows fired. Tayan was killed, and the Khitan army broke up and fled.

sentences.zh: 會曹利用自契丹使還，具得要領，又與其使者姚東之俱來，講和之議遂定。

translations.literal: As it happened Cao Liyong returned from his mission to the Khitan having fully grasped the essentials, and came together with their envoy Yao Dongzhi — the peace negotiations were then settled.
translations.idiomatic: As it happened, Cao Liyong returned from his mission to the Khitan having fully grasped the essentials, and came together with their envoy Yao Dongzhi. The peace negotiations were then settled.

sentences.zh: 歲遺契丹銀絹三十萬，朝論皆以為過。

translations.literal: Each year three hundred thousand taels of silver and bolts of silk were sent to the Khitan; court opinion generally considered this excessive.
translations.idiomatic: Each year three hundred thousand taels of silver and bolts of silk were sent to the Khitan, and court opinion generally considered the sum excessive.

sentences.zh: 士安曰：「不如此，契丹所顧不重，和事恐不能久。」

translations.literal: Shi'an said: "If it were not thus, what the Khitan cared about would not weigh heavily, and the peace might not last."
translations.idiomatic: Shi'an said, "If the payment were less, the Khitan would not value the peace highly, and the agreement might not last."

sentences.zh: 及罷兵，從還，乃按邊要選良守將易置之：雄州以李允則，定州馬知節，鎮州孫全照，保州楊延昭，它所擇用各得其任。

translations.literal: When the armies were disbanded and he returned with the Emperor, he then surveyed the border strongpoints and chose good defending generals, replacing them: Li Yunze for Xiong Prefecture, Ma Zhijie for Ding Prefecture, Sun Quanzhao for Zhen Prefecture, Yang Yanzhao for Bao Prefecture — elsewhere those he chose also each received fitting appointments.
translations.idiomatic: When the armies were disbanded and he returned with the Emperor, he surveyed the border strongpoints and appointed capable defending generals: Li Yunze at Xiong Prefecture, Ma Zhijie at Ding Prefecture, Sun Quanzhao at Zhen Prefecture, and Yang Yanzhao at Bao Prefecture. Elsewhere, those he chose also received fitting appointments.

sentences.zh: 令塞上得境外牛馬類者悉還之，通互市，除鐵禁，招流亡，廣儲蓄。

translations.literal: He ordered that cattle and horses of the sort captured beyond the border on the frontier all be returned, opened mutual markets, lifted the iron ban, summoned back refugees, and expanded reserves.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered that cattle and horses captured beyond the border be returned, opened mutual markets, lifted the iron ban, summoned back refugees, and expanded reserves.

sentences.zh: 未幾，夏州趙德明亦款塞內附。

translations.literal: Before long Zhao Deming of Xia Prefecture also offered sincere submission at the border and came within allegiance.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Zhao Deming of Xia Prefecture also offered sincere submission at the border and came within allegiance.

sentences.zh: 二方既定，中外略安。

translations.literal: With both frontiers settled, inside and outside were broadly at peace.
translations.idiomatic: With both frontiers settled, the realm was broadly at peace.

sentences.zh: 量時製法，次第施行。

translations.literal: Laws suited to the times were framed and implemented in sequence.
translations.idiomatic: Laws suited to the times were framed and implemented in sequence.

sentences.zh: 復置賢良方正、直言極諫等科，以廣取士。

translations.literal: The categories of Worthy and Upright, Straightforward Remonstrance, and the rest were restored to broaden recruitment of talent.
translations.idiomatic: The categories of Worthy and Upright, Straightforward Remonstrance, and the rest were restored to broaden recruitment of talent.

sentences.zh: 二年，章七八上，以病求免，優詔不允。

translations.literal: In the second year he submitted seven or eight memorials requesting dismissal on grounds of illness; gracious edicts did not grant this.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he submitted seven or eight memorials requesting dismissal on grounds of illness, but gracious edicts refused.

sentences.zh: 遣使敦諭，不得已，復起視事。

translations.literal: An envoy was sent to earnestly instruct him; having no choice, he rose again to attend to office.
translations.idiomatic: An envoy was sent to earnestly instruct him. Having no choice, he rose again to attend to office.

sentences.zh: 十月晨朝，至崇政殿廬，疾暴作，真宗步出臨視，已不能言。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, at the morning audience, when he reached the lodge of the Hall of Promoting Governance his illness suddenly seized him; Emperor Zhenzong walked out to look in on him — he could already no longer speak.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month, at the morning audience, when he reached the lodge of the Hall of Promoting Governance his illness suddenly seized him. Emperor Zhenzong walked out to look in on him, but Shi'an could already no longer speak.

sentences.zh: 詔內侍竇神寶以肩輿送歸第，卒，年六十八。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the inner attendant Dou Shenbao to carry him home in a sedan chair; he died, aged sixty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the inner attendant Dou Shenbao to carry him home in a sedan chair. He died at the age of sixty-eight.

sentences.zh: 車駕臨哭，廢朝五日，贈太傅、中書令，諡文簡。

translations.literal: The imperial carriage came in person to mourn; court was suspended for five days; posthumous gifts of Grand Tutor and Grand Counselor of the Secretariat were conferred; his posthumous title was Wenhjian.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor came in person to mourn. Court was suspended for five days. He was posthumously granted the titles Grand Tutor and Grand Counselor of the Secretariat, with the posthumous name Wenhjian.

sentences.zh: 以皇城使衛紹欽治葬，有司給鹵簿。

translations.literal: Wei Shaoqin, Commissioner of the Imperial City, was put in charge of the burial; the relevant offices supplied funeral regalia.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Shaoqin, Commissioner of the Imperial City, was put in charge of the burial, and the relevant offices supplied funeral regalia.

sentences.zh: 錄其子世長為太子中舍，慶長為大理寺丞，孫從古為將作監主簿。

translations.literal: His son Shichang was enrolled as Middle Gentleman of the Heir Apparent, Qingchang as Vice Director of the Court of Judicial Review, and his grandson Conggu as Secretary of the Directorate of Works.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shichang was enrolled as Middle Gentleman of the Heir Apparent, Qingchang as Vice Director of the Court of Judicial Review, and his grandson Conggu as Secretary of the Directorate of Works.

sentences.zh: 士安端方沉雅，有清識醞藉，美風采，善談吐，所至以嚴正稱。

translations.literal: Shi'an was dignified, sober, and refined, with clear judgment and cultivated reserve, fine bearing, and skilled discourse; wherever he went he was known for stern rectitude.
translations.idiomatic: Shi'an was dignified, sober, and refined, with clear judgment and cultivated reserve, fine bearing, and skilled discourse. Wherever he served he was known for stern rectitude.

sentences.zh: 年耆目眊，讀書不輟，手自讎校，或親繕寫。

translations.literal: In old age his eyes were dim, yet he never ceased reading, personally collating texts or even copying them by hand.
translations.idiomatic: In old age his eyes were dim, yet he never ceased reading, personally collating texts or even copying them by hand.

sentences.zh: 又精意詞翰，有文集三十卷。

translations.literal: He also applied himself diligently to literary composition and left a collected writings in thirty scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: He also applied himself diligently to literary composition and left collected writings in thirty scrolls.

sentences.zh: 嘗謂人曰：「僕仕宦無赫赫之譽，但力自規檢，庶幾寡過爾。」

translations.literal: He once told someone: "In official life I have had no resounding renown, but have only strained to govern myself — hoping to commit few faults, that is all."
translations.idiomatic: He once told someone, "In official life I have won no resounding renown. I have only tried to govern myself, hoping to commit few faults — that is all."

sentences.zh: 凡交游無黨援，唯王祐、呂端見引重，王旦、寇準、楊億相友善，王禹偁、陳彭年皆門人也。

translations.literal: In all his associations he had no factional backing; only Wang You and Lu Duan treated him with special esteem. He was friendly with Wang Dan, Kou Zhun, and Yang Yi; Wang Yucheng and Chen Pengnian were both his disciples.
translations.idiomatic: In all his associations he had no factional backing. Only Wang You and Lu Duan treated him with special esteem. He was friendly with Wang Dan, Kou Zhun, and Yang Yi; Wang Yucheng and Chen Pengnian were both his disciples.

sentences.zh: 禹偁，濟州人。

translations.literal: Yucheng was a native of Ji Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Yucheng was a native of Ji Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 幼時以事至士安官舍，士安識其非常童，留之，教以學，舉業日顯。

translations.literal: When young he came on business to Shi'an's official residence; Shi'an recognized him as an extraordinary child, kept him, taught him, and his examination work daily grew conspicuous.
translations.idiomatic: When young he came on business to Shi'an's official residence. Shi'an recognized him as an extraordinary child, kept him, and taught him, and his examination work grew conspicuous day by day.

sentences.zh: 後遂登科進用，更在士安前。

translations.literal: Later he passed the examinations and entered service, even ranking ahead of Shi'an.
translations.idiomatic: Later he passed the examinations and entered service, even ranking ahead of Shi'an.

sentences.zh: 及士安知制誥，其命乃禹偁詞也。

translations.literal: When Shi'an was made Drafting Edict Officer, the appointment decree was in Yucheng's wording.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi'an was made Drafting Edict Officer, the appointment decree was in Yucheng's wording.

sentences.zh: 士安沒後，真宗謂寇準等曰：「畢士安，善人也，事朕南府、東宮，以至輔相。

translations.literal: After Shi'an's death, Emperor Zhenzong said to Kou Zhun and others: "Bi Shi'an was a good man, serving me from the Southern Palace and Eastern Palace up to chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: After Shi'an's death, Emperor Zhenzong said to Kou Zhun and others, "Bi Shi'an was a good man. He served me from the Southern Palace and Eastern Palace all the way to chief minister.

sentences.zh: 飭躬慎行，有古人之風，遽此淪沒，深可悼惜。」

translations.literal: He disciplined himself and acted with care, bearing the air of the ancients — to perish so suddenly is deeply to be mourned."
translations.idiomatic: He disciplined himself and acted with care, bearing the air of the ancients. To perish so suddenly is deeply to be mourned."

sentences.zh: 及王旦為相，面奏：「陛下前稱畢士安清慎如古人，在位聞之感歎。

translations.literal: When Wang Dan became chief minister he addressed the throne: "Your Majesty formerly praised Bi Shi'an as pure and cautious like the ancients; hearing this while in office I was moved to sigh.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Dan became chief minister he addressed the throne, "Your Majesty formerly praised Bi Shi'an as pure and cautious like the ancients. Hearing this while in office I was moved to sigh.

sentences.zh: 仕至輔相，而四方無田園居第，沒未終喪，家用已屈，真不負陛下所知。
