translations.literal: He rose to chief minister yet had no estate or residence anywhere in the realm; before mourning was finished his household funds were exhausted — truly he did not betray Your Majesty's recognition.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to chief minister yet had no estate or residence anywhere in the realm. Before mourning was finished his household funds were exhausted — truly he did not betray Your Majesty's recognition.

sentences.zh: 然使其家假貸為生，宜有以周之者，竊謂當出上恩，非臣敢為私惠。」

translations.literal: Yet if his family must borrow to live, there ought to be means to assist them — I privately consider that imperial grace should be extended; this is not something your subject dares offer as private favor."
translations.idiomatic: Yet if his family must borrow to live, they ought to receive assistance. I privately believe imperial grace should be extended — this is not something your subject dares offer as private favor."

sentences.zh: 真宗感歎，賜白金五千兩。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhenzong was moved and sighed, and bestowed five thousand taels of white silver.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhenzong was deeply moved and granted five thousand taels of silver.

sentences.zh: 子世長至衛尉卿，慶長至大府卿。

translations.literal: His son Shichang rose to Chamberlain for Imperial Insignia; Qingchang rose to Chamberlain for the Grand Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shichang rose to Chamberlain for Imperial Insignia, and Qingchang to Chamberlain for the Grand Treasury.

sentences.zh: 孫從善光祿少卿，從古駕部郎中，從厚、從誨檢校水部員外郎，從簡博羅令，從道殿中丞，從範山南西道節度推官，從益太常寺太祝，從周朝散郎、知洋州。

translations.literal: His grandsons: Congshan became Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments; Conggu was Director of the Transport Bureau; Conghou and Conghui were Supernumerary Vice Directors of the Ministry of Works; Congjian was magistrate of Boluo; Congdao was Palace Censor; Congfan was administrative aide of the Shannan West Circuit military commissioner; Congyi was Chief Sacrificial Officer of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; Congzhou was Gentleman for Miscellaneous Uses and prefect of Yang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Among his grandsons, Congshan became Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments and Conggu Director of the Transport Bureau; Conghou and Conghui served as Supernumerary Vice Directors of the Ministry of Works; Congjian as magistrate of Boluo; Congdao as Palace Censor; Congfan as aide to the military commissioner of Shannan West Circuit; Congyi as Chief Sacrificial Officer of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; and Congzhou as Gentleman for Miscellaneous Uses and prefect of Yang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 曾孫仲達、仲偃仕至郡守，仲衍、仲游、仲愈。

translations.literal: Among his great-grandsons, Zhongda and Zhongyan rose to prefect; also Zhong Yan, Zhong You, and Zhong Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Among his great-grandsons, Zhongda and Zhongyan became prefects; Zhong Yan, Zhong You, and Zhong Yu are also counted among them.

sentences.zh: 〈曾孫〉

translations.literal: 〈Great-Grandsons〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Great-Grandsons〉

sentences.zh: 仲衍

translations.literal: Zhong Yan
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Yan

sentences.zh: 仲衍，字夷仲，以蔭為陽翟主簿。

translations.literal: Zhong Yan, courtesy name Yizhong, entered office by yin privilege as registrar of Yangdi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Yan, courtesy name Yizhong, received appointment through hereditary privilege as registrar of Yangdi County.

sentences.zh: 張昪，縣人也，方鎮許，請於朝，欲興鄉校。

translations.literal: Zhang Bian, a native of the county, was then administering Xu and memorialized the court, wishing to establish a local school.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Bian, a native of the county, was then governing Xu Prefecture. He memorialized the court seeking to establish a local school.

sentences.zh: 既具材計工，又聽民自以其力輸助。

translations.literal: Once materials were prepared and labor calculated, the people were also allowed to contribute labor of their own accord.
translations.idiomatic: After materials were readied and labor costs estimated, the people were also permitted to volunteer their own labor.

sentences.zh: 邑子馬宏以口舌橫閭里，謾謂諸豪曰：「張公興學，而縣令乃因以取諸民，由十百而至千萬未已也，君將不堪。

translations.literal: Ma Hong, a man of the locality, domineered the neighborhood with glib talk and deceived the local magnates, saying: "Master Zhang is building a school, but the magistrate will use this to extract from the people — from tens and hundreds up to thousands and ten thousands without end. You will not be able to bear it.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Hong, a local man who lorded over the neighborhood with his tongue, lied to the gentry magnates: "Master Zhang is founding a school, but the magistrate will use it to squeeze the people — from tens and hundreds to thousands and millions without end. You will not be able to stand it.

sentences.zh: 誠捐百金予我，我能止役。」

translations.literal: If you truly give me a hundred in gold, I can stop the corvée."
translations.idiomatic: Give me a hundred in gold in earnest, and I can halt the labor levy."

sentences.zh: 豪信其能，予百金。

translations.literal: The magnates believed he could do it and gave him a hundred in gold.
translations.idiomatic: The magnates believed him and paid him a hundred in gold.

sentences.zh: 宏即詣府宣言：「縣吏盡私為學之費，又將賦於民。」

translations.literal: Hong went straight to the prefecture and proclaimed: "The county clerks are all privately diverting school funds and will again levy taxes on the people."
translations.idiomatic: Hong went at once to the prefecture and declared: "The county clerks are embezzling the school funds and will levy taxes on the people again."

sentences.zh: 昪果疑焉，敕縣且止，又揭其事於道。

translations.literal: Bian indeed grew suspicious, ordered the county to halt for the time being, and also posted the matter along the roads.
translations.idiomatic: Bian did grow suspicious, ordered the county to suspend work for the time being, and posted the accusation along the roads.

sentences.zh: 令欲上疏辯，仲衍曰：「亡益也，不如取宏治之，不辯自直矣。」

translations.literal: The magistrate wished to memorialize in defense; Zhong Yan said: "It will do no good. Better to seize Hong and punish him — without arguing, your innocence will clear itself."
translations.idiomatic: The magistrate wanted to submit a memorial in his own defense. Zhong Yan said, "That will do no good. Better to arrest Hong and try him — without arguing, your innocence will speak for itself."

sentences.zh: 會攝縣事，即逮捕驗治，五日得其姦，言於昪，流宏鄧州，一縣相賀。

translations.literal: As it happened he was acting magistrate; he immediately arrested and investigated, and within five days uncovered the fraud. He reported to Bian and had Hong exiled to Deng Prefecture; the whole county congratulated one another.
translations.idiomatic: As it happened he was acting magistrate. He arrested Hong at once and investigated; within five days the fraud was exposed. He reported to Bian, and Hong was exiled to Deng Prefecture. The whole county rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 給事中張問居里中，謂仲衍曰：「諺云『鋤一惡，長十善』，君之謂也。」

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Zhang Wen, living in the same district, told Zhong Yan: "The proverb says, 'Uproot one evil and ten virtues grow' — that describes you."
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Zhang Wen, a neighbor in the district, said to Zhong Yan, "The proverb runs, 'Uproot one evil and ten virtues grow.' That is you."

sentences.zh: 舉進士中第，調沈丘令。

translations.literal: He passed the civil service examination and was assigned magistrate of Shenqiu.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination and was posted as magistrate of Shenqiu.

sentences.zh: 歐陽修、呂公著薦之，入司農為主簿，升丞。

translations.literal: Ouyang Xiu and Lü Gongzhu recommended him; he entered the Ministry of Revenue as registrar and was promoted to vice director.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended by Ouyang Xiu and Lü Gongzhu, he entered the Ministry of Revenue as registrar and was promoted to vice director.

sentences.zh: 吳充引為中書檢正。

translations.literal: Wu Chong brought him in as collating editor of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Chong appointed him collating editor of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 奉使契丹，宴射連破的，眾驚異之。

translations.literal: On mission to the Khitan, at a banquet archery contest he hit the target repeatedly; all were astonished.
translations.idiomatic: On an embassy to the Khitan, at a banquet archery contest he hit the target again and again, to everyone's astonishment.

sentences.zh: 且偉其姿容，密使人取其衣為度，制服以賜。

translations.literal: Moreover they admired his bearing; secretly they sent someone to take measurements of his clothes, made robes to fit, and bestowed them.
translations.idiomatic: They also admired his stature and bearing. Secretly they had his garments measured, had robes made to fit, and bestowed them on him.

sentences.zh: 時預其元會，盡能記其朝儀節奏，圖畫歸獻。

translations.literal: He then attended their New Year's assembly, memorized every detail of court ritual and its cadence, and returned with diagrams to present.
translations.idiomatic: He attended their New Year assembly, memorized the full order and rhythm of court ritual, and returned with illustrated records to present at court.

sentences.zh: 後錢勰出使，契丹主猶問：「畢少卿何官？

translations.literal: Later when Qian Yi went on mission, the Khitan ruler still asked: "What office does Vice Director Bi hold?
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Qian Yi went on embassy, the Khitan ruler still asked, "What office does Vice Director Bi hold?

sentences.zh: 今安在？」

translations.literal: Where is he now?"
translations.idiomatic: Where is he now?"

sentences.zh: 王珪與充不相能，以仲衍為充所用，數求罪過欲傷之，卒無可乘，但留滯不遷。

translations.literal: Wang Gui and Wu Chong were mutually hostile; because Zhong Yan was employed by Chong, Gui repeatedly sought faults hoping to harm him, but in the end found none to exploit — only kept him stuck without promotion.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Gui and Wu Chong were at odds. Because Zhong Yan was Wu Chong's man, Gui repeatedly hunted for faults with which to injure him but never found an opening — he could only leave him stuck without promotion.

sentences.zh: 經四年，乃以秘閣校理同知太常禮院，為官制局檢討官，制文字千萬計，區別分類，損益刪補，皆曲盡其當。

translations.literal: After four years he was appointed collating editor of the Secretariat Archive and concurrent administrator of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices ritual office; as review officer of the office-reform bureau he drafted texts numbering in the tens of millions of characters — classifying, revising, adding and cutting — all to perfect appropriateness.
translations.idiomatic: After four years he was made collating editor of the Secretariat Archive and concurrent administrator of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices ritual office, and served as review officer of the office-reform bureau. He drafted texts numbering in the tens of millions of characters, sorting, revising, adding and deleting until every detail was exactly right.

sentences.zh: 凡從中問其事，必須仲衍然後報，他人不知也。

translations.literal: Whenever the court inquired about such matters, the reply had to come from Zhong Yan before it was sent; others did not know.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the court inquired about such matters, the answer had to come from Zhong Yan before a reply could be sent — no one else knew the material.

sentences.zh: 撰《中書備對》三十卷，士大夫家爭傳其書。

translations.literal: He compiled thirty fascicles of Reference Replies for the Secretariat; gentry households competed to circulate the book.
translations.idiomatic: He compiled thirty fascicles of Reference Replies for the Secretariat, and scholar-official households competed to copy and circulate the work.

sentences.zh: 高麗使入貢，詔館之。

translations.literal: When Goryeo envoys came to pay tribute, an edict ordered them lodged with him.
translations.idiomatic: When Goryeo envoys arrived with tribute, an edict directed that they be lodged under his care.

sentences.zh: 上元夕，與使者宴東闕下，作詩誦聖德，神宗次韻賜焉，當時以為寵。

translations.literal: On Lantern Festival night he feasted the envoys below the eastern gate, composed poetry praising imperial virtue; Emperor Shenzong responded in matching rhymes — at the time this was regarded as special favor.
translations.idiomatic: On Lantern Festival night he feasted the envoys below the eastern gate and composed poetry praising imperial virtue. Emperor Shenzong responded in matching rhymes — at the time this was taken as high favor.

sentences.zh: 官制行，帝自擢起居郎，王珪留除命，謂為太峻，爭於前。

translations.literal: When the new official system took effect, the Emperor personally promoted him to Diary Reader; Wang Gui withheld the appointment decree, saying the rank was too lofty, and argued before the throne.
translations.idiomatic: When the new official system took effect, the Emperor personally promoted him to Diary Reader. Wang Gui withheld the appointment decree, calling the rank too steep, and argued the point before the throne.

sentences.zh: 帝連稱曰：「是當得爾。」

translations.literal: The Emperor repeatedly said: "He deserves exactly this."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said again and again, "He deserves exactly this."

sentences.zh: 未幾，暴得疾，一夕卒，年四十三。

translations.literal: Before long he suddenly fell ill and died in a single night, aged forty-three.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he fell suddenly ill and died overnight, aged forty-three.

sentences.zh: 帝遣中使唁其家，賻錢五十萬。

translations.literal: The Emperor sent a palace envoy to condole with his family and granted fifty thousand in funeral money.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor sent a palace envoy to condole with his family and granted fifty thousand in funeral assistance.

sentences.zh: 〈曾孫〉

translations.literal: 〈Great-Grandsons〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Great-Grandsons〉

sentences.zh: 仲游

translations.literal: Zhong You
translations.idiomatic: Zhong You

sentences.zh: 仲游，字公叔，與仲衍同登第，調壽丘柘城主簿、羅山令、環慶轉運司干辦公事。

translations.literal: Zhong You, courtesy name Gongshu, passed the examinations together with Zhong Yan; he was assigned registrar of Shouqiu and Zhecheng, magistrate of Luoshan, and staff officer of the Huanqing Transport Commission.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong You, courtesy name Gongshu, passed the examinations together with Zhong Yan. He served as registrar of Shouqiu and Zhecheng, magistrate of Luoshan, and staff officer on the Huanqing Transport Commission.

sentences.zh: 從高遵裕西征，運期迫遽，陝西八十縣饋輓之夫三十萬，一旦悉集，轉運使范純粹、李察度受其賦而給之食，必曠日乃可。

translations.literal: Following Gao Zunyu's western campaign, transport deadlines were urgent; three hundred thousand corvée haulers from eighty counties of Shaanxi gathered all at once. Transport commissioners Fan Chunzui and Li Cha planned to accept their labor dues and then ration food — it would necessarily take many days.
translations.idiomatic: When he followed Gao Zunyu on the western campaign, transport deadlines were tight. Three hundred thousand corvée haulers from eighty Shaanxi counties gathered overnight. Transport commissioners Fan Chunzui and Li Cha intended to collect their labor dues first and only then issue rations — which would necessarily take days.

sentences.zh: 會僚屬議，皆不知所為，以諉仲游。

translations.literal: When colleagues met to discuss, none knew what to do and shifted the responsibility to Zhong You.
translations.idiomatic: When the staff met to discuss the crisis, no one knew what to do and pushed the problem onto Zhong You.

sentences.zh: 仲游集諸縣吏，令先效金帛緡錢之最，戒勿啟扃鐍，共簿其名數以為質，預飭其斛量數千，洞撤倉庾牆壁，使贏糧者至其所，人自𣂏槩，輸其半而以半自給，不終朝霍然而散。

translations.literal: Zhong You assembled the county clerks, had them first pledge their utmost in gold, silk, and cash, warned them not to break seals, and jointly recorded names and amounts as surety. He pre-positioned thousands of bushel measures, opened granaries and tore down walls, so those bringing surplus grain could come directly; each man measured his own ration with the grain measure, paid half in grain and took half as self-supply — before noon all dispersed in a flash.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong You gathered the county clerks, had each pledge his maximum in gold, silk, and cash, forbade them to break seals, and recorded all names and amounts as bond. He prepared thousands of bushel measures in advance, opened the granaries and knocked down the walls so grain carriers could reach them directly. Each man measured his own ration, turned in half and kept half for himself — and before noon the whole host had dispersed.

sentences.zh: 翌日，大軍遂行。

translations.literal: The next day the great army set out.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the main army marched.

sentences.zh: 純粹、察歎且謝曰：「非君幾敗吾事。」

translations.literal: Chunzui and Cha sighed and thanked him: "Without you we would nearly have ruined the campaign."
translations.idiomatic: Chunzui and Cha sighed and thanked him: "Without you we would almost have ruined the whole operation."

sentences.zh: 元祐初，為軍器衛尉丞。

translations.literal: At the start of the Yuanyou era he served as Vice Director of the Armory and Ceremonials.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Yuanyou era he served as Vice Director of the Armory and Ceremonials.

sentences.zh: 召試學士院，同策問者九人，乃黃庭堅、張耒、晁補之輩。

translations.literal: Summoned to the Hanlin examination hall; nine others took the policy questions with him, including Huang Tingjian, Zhang Lei, and Chao Buzhi.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to the Hanlin examination hall. Nine others answered the policy questions with him, among them Huang Tingjian, Zhang Lei, and Chao Buzhi.

sentences.zh: 蘇軾異其文，擢為第一。

translations.literal: Su Shi admired his essay and ranked him first.
translations.idiomatic: Su Shi was struck by his essay and placed him first.

sentences.zh: 加集賢校理、開封府推官，出提點河東路刑獄。

translations.literal: He was additionally made collating editor of the Hall of Assembled Worthies and investigating officer of Kaifeng prefecture, then sent out as judicial intendant of Hedong East Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was further appointed collating editor of the Hall of Assembled Worthies and investigating officer of Kaifeng prefecture, then sent out as judicial intendant of Hedong East Circuit.

sentences.zh: 韓縝以故相在太原，按視如列郡，縝奴告有卒剽其衣於公堂之側，縝怒，將置卒於理。

translations.literal: Han Zhen, as a former chief minister, was in Taiyuan and inspected affairs as if he were merely a regular prefect. A slave of Zhen reported that a soldier had robbed his clothes beside the public hall; Zhen was furious and would have prosecuted the soldier.
translations.idiomatic: Han Zhen, a former chief minister, was in Taiyuan and inspected the circuit as though it were an ordinary prefecture. One of Zhen's slaves reported that a soldier had stripped him of his clothes beside the public hall. Zhen was enraged and meant to prosecute the soldier.

sentences.zh: 仲游曰：「奴衣服鮮薄而敢掠之於帥牙，非人情也。」

translations.literal: Zhong You said: "The slave's clothes were fine and thin — yet he dares claim robbery at the commander's gate? That is not human nature."
translations.idiomatic: Zhong You said, "The slave's clothes were fine and light — yet he claims robbery at the commander's very gate? That is not credible."

sentences.zh: 取以付獄治，卒得免。

translations.literal: He took the case for prison investigation; the soldier was exonerated.
translations.idiomatic: He took the slave into custody for investigation, and the soldier was cleared.

sentences.zh: 太原銅器名天下，獨不市一物，懼人以為矯也，且行，買二茶匕而去。

translations.literal: Taiyuan bronze ware was famed throughout the realm, yet he alone bought not a single item, fearing people would think it pretense; when about to leave he bought two tea spoons and departed.
translations.idiomatic: Taiyuan bronze was famed throughout the realm, yet he alone bought nothing, fearing people would call it affectation. As he was about to leave, he bought two tea spoons and went.

sentences.zh: 縝曰：「如公叔可謂真清矣。」

translations.literal: Zhen said: "One like Gongshu may truly be called pure."
translations.idiomatic: Zhen said, "A man like Gongshu may truly be called incorruptible."

sentences.zh: 召拜職方、司勳二員外郎，改秘閣校理、知耀州。

translations.literal: Summoned and appointed Vice Director of both the Bureau of Posts and the Bureau of Honors; transferred to collating editor of the Secretariat Archive and prefect of Yao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned and appointed Vice Director of both the Bureau of Posts and the Bureau of Honors, then transferred to collating editor of the Secretariat Archive and prefect of Yao Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 是歲大旱，仲游先民之未飢，揭喻境內曰：「郡振施與平糴若干萬石。」

translations.literal: That year there was great drought; before the people grew hungry Zhong You posted notices throughout the jurisdiction: "The prefecture will distribute relief and sell grain at fair price — several millions of bushels."
translations.idiomatic: That year brought severe drought. Before the people went hungry, Zhong You posted notices throughout the prefecture: "The commandery will distribute relief grain and sell at fair price — several million bushels in all."

sentences.zh: 實虛張其數。

translations.literal: In fact he grossly inflated the figure.
translations.idiomatic: In fact he had greatly inflated the number.

sentences.zh: 富室知有備，亦相勸發廩。

translations.literal: Wealthy households, knowing reserves existed, also urged one another to open their granaries.
translations.idiomatic: Wealthy households, seeing that reserves were in place, also urged one another to open their storehouses.

sentences.zh: 凡民就食者十七萬九千口，無一人去其鄉。

translations.literal: In all, 179,000 people received food; not one left his home district.
translations.idiomatic: In all, 179,000 people received rations, and not one abandoned his home district.

sentences.zh: 徽宗時，歷知鄭、鄆二州，京東、淮南轉運副使。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Huizong he successively governed Zheng and Yun prefectures and served as deputy transport commissioner of Jingdong and Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Huizong he successively governed Zheng and Yun prefectures and served as deputy transport commissioner for Jingdong and Huainan.

sentences.zh: 入為吏部郎中，言孔子廟自顏回以降，皆爵命於朝，冠冕居正，而子鯉、孫伋乃野服幅巾以祭，為不稱。

translations.literal: Entering office as Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel, he said that in Confucius's temple from Yan Hui downward all had court ranks and wore official caps in the central place, yet Zili and Sun Ji wore plain clothes and headcloths to sacrifice — this was unfitting.
translations.idiomatic: After entering office as Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel, he observed that in Confucius's temple everyone from Yan Hui downward held court rank and wore official caps in the central place, while Zili and Sun Ji sacrificed in plain dress and headcloths — which he said was unfitting.

sentences.zh: 詔皆追侯之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered all to be posthumously ennobled as marquises.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered that they all be posthumously ennobled as marquises.

sentences.zh: 仲游早受知於司馬光、呂公著，不及用。

translations.literal: Zhong You had early won recognition from Sima Guang and Lü Gongzhu, but was not employed in time.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong You had won early recognition from Sima Guang and Lü Gongzhu, yet was never put to use in time.

sentences.zh: 范純仁尤知之，當國時，又適居母喪，故未嘗得尺寸進。

translations.literal: Fan Chunren knew him especially well; when he held power Zhong You happened to be in mourning for his mother, so he never gained the slightest advancement.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Chunren knew him especially well, but when Chunren held power Zhong You happened to be in mourning for his mother, so he never received even the smallest promotion.

sentences.zh: 然亦墮黨籍，坎𡒄散秩而終，年七十五。

translations.literal: Nevertheless he also fell into the faction list, ended his days in frustrated minor posts, aged seventy-five.
translations.idiomatic: He nevertheless fell into the faction list as well and ended his days in obstructed, minor posts, dying at seventy-five.

sentences.zh: 仲游為文切於事理而有根柢，不為浮誇詭誕、戲弄不莊之語。

translations.literal: Zhong You's writing cut to the logic of affairs and had solid foundations; he did not use inflated, strange, or playful irreverent language.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong You's prose cut straight to the logic of affairs and rested on solid foundations. He wrote none of the inflated, bizarre, or flippantly irreverent language common in his day.

sentences.zh: 蘇軾在館閣，頗以言語文章規切時政。

translations.literal: Su Shi, while in the archives institute, often used speech and essays to admonish current policy.
translations.idiomatic: While serving in the Hanlin archives, Su Shi often used speech and essays to criticize current policy.

sentences.zh: 仲游憂其及禍，貽書戒之曰：

translations.literal: Zhong You, fearing he would meet disaster, sent a letter warning him:
translations.idiomatic: Fearing that disaster would reach him, Zhong You sent a letter of warning:

sentences.zh: 「孟軻不得已而後辯，孔子欲無言，古人所以精謀極慮，固功業而養壽命者，未嘗不出乎此。

translations.literal: "Mencius argued only when he could not do otherwise; Confucius wished to be without words. The ancients who through deep planning and utmost deliberation secured their achievements and preserved their lives never departed from this principle.
translations.idiomatic: "Mencius argued only when he could not do otherwise; Confucius wished to be without words. Among the ancients, those who through careful planning secured their achievements and preserved their lives never strayed from this principle.

sentences.zh: 君自立朝以來，禍福利害繫身者未嘗言，顧直惜其言爾。

translations.literal: Since you entered court, you have never spoken of fortune or misfortune touching your own person — you have merely been sparing of words.
translations.idiomatic: Since you entered court you have never spoken of fortune or misfortune touching your own person — you have simply been sparing of words.

sentences.zh: 夫言語之累，不特出口者為言，其形於詩歌、贊於賦頌、託於碑銘、著於序記者，亦語言也。

translations.literal: The burden of language is not limited to what leaves the mouth: what takes shape in songs, appears in rhapsodies and eulogies, is entrusted to stele inscriptions, or is set down in prefaces and records — that too is language.
translations.idiomatic: The burden of language is not limited to what leaves the mouth. What takes shape in song, appears in rhapsodies and eulogies, is entrusted to stele inscriptions, or is set down in prefaces and records — that too is language.

sentences.zh: 今知畏於口而未畏於文，是其所是則見是者喜，非其所非則蒙非者怨；

translations.literal: Now you fear the mouth but not the written word. When you affirm what others affirm, those who see the affirmation rejoice; when you deny what others deny, those who are denied grow resentful;
translations.idiomatic: Now you fear the mouth but not the written word. When you affirm what others affirm, those who see the affirmation rejoice; when you deny what others deny, those who are denied grow resentful;

sentences.zh: 喜者未能濟君之謀，而怨者或已敗君之事矣。

translations.literal: those who rejoice cannot advance your designs, while those who resent you may already have ruined your affairs.
translations.idiomatic: those who rejoice cannot advance your designs, while those who resent you may already have ruined your affairs.

sentences.zh: 天下論君之文，如孫臏之用兵，扁鵲之醫疾，固所指名者矣。

translations.literal: The realm discusses your writing as they discuss Sun Bin's use of arms or Bian Que's treatment of illness — your targets are already named.
translations.idiomatic: The realm reads your writing as it reads Sun Bin's warfare or Bian Que's medicine — your targets are already plain.

sentences.zh: 雖無是非之言，猶有是非之疑，又況其有耶？

translations.literal: Even without words of right and wrong, there is still suspicion of right and wrong — how much more when there truly are such words?
translations.idiomatic: Even without explicit words of right and wrong, suspicion of right and wrong remains — how much more when such words are truly there?

sentences.zh: 官非諫臣，職非御史，而非是人所未是，危身觸諱以游其間，殆猶抱石而救溺也。」

translations.literal: Your office is not that of remonstrance officer, your duty not that of censor — yet you deny what others have not denied and risk your person by touching taboos to move among them. That is nearly like embracing a stone to save a drowning man."
translations.idiomatic: Your office is not that of remonstrance officer, your duty not that of censor — yet you deny what others have not denied and risk your person by touching taboos as you move among them. That is nearly like embracing a stone to save a drowning man."

sentences.zh: 司馬光為政，反王安石所為，仲游予之書曰：

translations.literal: When Sima Guang took power and reversed what Wang Anshi had done, Zhong You sent him a letter saying:
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Guang took power and reversed Wang Anshi's policies, Zhong You sent him a letter saying:

sentences.zh: 「昔安石以興作之說動先帝，而患財之不足也，故凡政之可以得民財者無不用。

translations.literal: "In the past Anshi moved the late Emperor with talk of grand undertakings and worried that funds were insufficient; therefore every policy that could draw wealth from the people was used.
translations.idiomatic: "In the past Wang Anshi moved the late Emperor with talk of grand undertakings and worried that funds were insufficient; therefore every policy that could draw wealth from the people was put to use.

sentences.zh: 蓋散青苗、置市易、斂役錢、變鹽法者，事也；

translations.literal: Dispersing Green Sprouts loans, establishing the Market Exchange, collecting labor-exemption money, and reforming the salt laws — these were matters;
translations.idiomatic: Dispersing Green Sprouts loans, establishing the Market Exchange, collecting labor-exemption money, and reforming the salt laws — these were matters;

sentences.zh: 而欲興作、患不足者，情也。

translations.literal: the wish to undertake grand projects and the anxiety over insufficiency were dispositions.
translations.idiomatic: the wish to undertake grand projects and the anxiety over insufficiency were dispositions.

sentences.zh: 苟未能杜其興作之情，而徒欲禁其散斂變置之事，是以百說而百不行。

translations.literal: If one cannot stop the disposition toward grand undertakings and merely tries to forbid the matters of dispersing, collecting, and rearranging revenue, then a hundred proposals will be made and a hundred will fail.
translations.idiomatic: If one cannot stop the disposition toward grand undertakings and merely tries to forbid the matters of dispersing, collecting, and rearranging revenue, then a hundred proposals will be made and a hundred will fail.

sentences.zh: 今遂廢青苗，罷市易，蠲役錢，去鹽法，凡號為利而傷民者，一掃而更之，則向來用事於新法者必不喜矣。

translations.literal: Now Green Sprouts is abolished, the Market Exchange halted, labor-exemption money remitted, and the salt laws removed — every measure called profit at the people's expense is swept away and replaced. Then those who formerly wielded the New Policies will surely be displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Now Green Sprouts is abolished, the Market Exchange halted, labor-exemption money remitted, and the salt laws removed — every measure called profit at the people's expense is swept away and replaced. Those who formerly wielded the New Policies will surely be displeased.

sentences.zh: 不喜之人，必不但曰『青苗不可廢，市易不可罷，役錢不可蠲，鹽法不可去』，必操不足之情，言不足之事，以動上意，雖致石人而使聽之，猶將動也。

translations.literal: Those who are displeased will not merely say, "Green Sprouts cannot be abolished, the Market Exchange cannot be halted, labor-exemption money cannot be remitted, the salt laws cannot be removed." They will seize on the disposition of insufficiency and speak of matters of insufficiency to move the sovereign's mind — even if a stone man were made to listen, he would still be moved.
translations.idiomatic: Those who are displeased will not merely say, "Green Sprouts cannot be abolished, the Market Exchange cannot be halted, labor-exemption money cannot be remitted, the salt laws cannot be removed." They will seize on the disposition of insufficiency and speak of matters of insufficiency to move the sovereign's mind — even if a stone man were made to listen, he would still be moved.

sentences.zh: 如是，則廢者可復散，罷者可復置，蠲者可復斂，去者可復存矣。

translations.literal: If so, what was abolished can again be dispersed, what was halted can again be established, what was remitted can again be collected, and what was removed can again survive.
translations.idiomatic: If so, what was abolished can again be dispersed, what was halted can again be established, what was remitted can again be collected, and what was removed can again survive.

sentences.zh: 則不足之情，可不預治哉？

translations.literal: Then should not the disposition of insufficiency be treated in advance?
translations.idiomatic: Should not the disposition of insufficiency be treated in advance?

sentences.zh: 為今之策，當大舉天下之計，深明出入之數，以諸路所積之錢粟一歸地官，使經費可支二十年之用。

translations.literal: The policy for today should be to take comprehensive account of the realm's finances, clarify revenues and expenditures in depth, and gather all cash and grain accumulated in the circuits under the Ministry of Revenue so that operating expenses can be met for twenty years.
translations.idiomatic: The policy for today should be to take comprehensive account of the realm's finances, clarify revenues and expenditures in depth, and gather all cash and grain accumulated in the circuits under the Ministry of Revenue so that operating expenses can be met for twenty years.

sentences.zh: 數年之間，又將十倍於今日。

translations.literal: Within a few years the stores will again be ten times what they are today.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few years the stores will again be ten times what they are today.

sentences.zh: 使天子曉然知天下之餘於財也，則不足之論不得陳於前，然後所論新法者，始可永罷而不可行矣。

translations.literal: If the Son of Heaven clearly knows that the realm abounds in wealth, then talk of insufficiency cannot be set before him — only then can the New Policies discussed above be permanently halted and kept from execution.
translations.idiomatic: If the Son of Heaven clearly sees that the realm abounds in wealth, then talk of insufficiency cannot be set before him — only then can the New Policies be permanently halted and kept from execution.

sentences.zh: 昔安石之居位也，中外莫非其人，故其法能行。

translations.literal: When Anshi held office, inside and outside the court there were none who were not his men; therefore his laws could be enforced.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Anshi held office, inside and outside the court there were almost none who were not his men; therefore his laws could be enforced.

sentences.zh: 今欲救前日之敝，而左右侍從、職司、使者，十有七八皆安石之徒，雖起二三舊臣，用六七君子，然累百之中存基十數，烏在其勢之可為也。

translations.literal: Now you wish to remedy the abuses of earlier days, yet seven or eight tenths of those at the sovereign's side, in office, and on commission are Anshi's followers. Even if two or three old ministers are raised up and six or seven gentlemen employed, of several hundred only a dozen or so remain — how can the situation be workable?
translations.idiomatic: Now you wish to remedy the abuses of earlier days, yet seven or eight tenths of those at the sovereign's side, in office, and on commission are Wang Anshi's followers. Even if two or three old ministers are raised up and six or seven gentlemen employed, of several hundred only a dozen or so remain — how can the situation be workable?

sentences.zh: 勢未可為而欲為之，則青苗雖廢將復散，況未廢乎？

translations.literal: When the situation is not workable yet one tries to work it, then even if Green Sprouts is abolished it will again be dispersed — how much more when it is not yet abolished?
translations.idiomatic: When the situation is not workable yet one tries to work it, then even if Green Sprouts is abolished it will again be dispersed — how much more when it is not yet abolished?

sentences.zh: 市易雖罷且復置，況未罷乎？

translations.literal: Even if the Market Exchange is halted it will again be established — how much more when it is not yet halted?
translations.idiomatic: Even if the Market Exchange is halted it will again be established — how much more when it is not yet halted?

sentences.zh: 役錢、鹽法亦莫不然。

translations.literal: Labor-exemption money and the salt laws are no different.
translations.idiomatic: Labor-exemption money and the salt laws are no different.

sentences.zh: 以此救前日之敝，如人久病而少間，其父子兄弟喜見顏色而未敢賀者，以其病之猶在也。」

translations.literal: To remedy the abuses of earlier days in this way is like a man long ill who shows a little improvement: father, sons, and brothers are glad to see color return to his face yet dare not congratulate him, because the illness is still there."
translations.idiomatic: To remedy the abuses of earlier days in this way is like a man long ill who shows a little improvement: father, sons, and brothers are glad to see color return to his face yet dare not congratulate him, because the illness is still there."

sentences.zh: 光、軾得書聳然，竟如其慮。

translations.literal: Guang and Shi received the letter and started; in the end it happened exactly as he had foreseen.
translations.idiomatic: Guang and Shi received the letter and started — in the end events unfolded exactly as he had foreseen.

sentences.zh: 仲愈歷國子監丞、諸王府侍講、知鳳翔府，坐兄仲游陷黨籍，例廢黜。

translations.literal: Zhong Yu served as vice director of the Directorate of Education, lecturer in the princes' households, and prefect of Fengxiang; because his elder brother Zhong You fell into the faction list he was dismissed by precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Yu served as vice director of the Directorate of Education, lecturer in the princes' households, and prefect of Fengxiang. Because his elder brother Zhong You fell into the faction list, he was dismissed by precedent.

sentences.zh: 徽宗曰：「畢仲衍被遇先帝，可除罪籍。」

translations.literal: Emperor Huizong said: "Bi Zhongyan received favor from the late Emperor; he may be removed from the proscribed registry."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Huizong said, "Bi Zhongyan received favor from the late Emperor; he may be removed from the proscribed registry."

sentences.zh: 以仲愈為都官郎中，擢秘書少監，卒。

translations.literal: Zhong Yu was appointed Vice Director of the Ministry of Justice, promoted to Vice Director of the Secretariat, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Yu was appointed Vice Director of the Ministry of Justice, promoted to Vice Director of the Secretariat, and died.

sentences.zh: 寇準，字平仲，華州下邽人也。

translations.literal: Kou Zhun, courtesy name Pingzhong, was a native of Xiayu in Hua Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Kou Zhun, courtesy name Pingzhong, was a native of Xiayu in Hua Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父相，晉開運中，應辟為魏王府記室參軍。

translations.literal: His father Xiang, during the Kaiyun era of Later Jin, accepted summons as recorder of the Prince of Wei's establishment.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xiang, during the Kaiyun era of Later Jin, accepted summons as recorder of the Prince of Wei's establishment.

sentences.zh: 準少英邁，通《春秋》三傳。

translations.literal: Zhun in youth was brilliant and far-reaching, mastering the three commentaries on the Spring and Autumn Annals.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Kou Zhun was brilliant and far-reaching, mastering the three commentaries on the Spring and Autumn Annals.

sentences.zh: 年十九，舉進士。

translations.literal: At nineteen he passed the civil service examination.
translations.idiomatic: At nineteen he passed the civil service examination.

sentences.zh: 太宗取人，多臨軒顧問，年少者往往罷去。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong in selecting men often questioned them face-to-face at the imperial hall. Those who were young were often dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: In selecting officials, Emperor Taizong often questioned candidates in person at the imperial hall. Young men were frequently sent away.

sentences.zh: 或教準增年，答曰：「準方進取，可欺君邪？」

translations.literal: Some advised Zhun to add to his age. He replied: "Zhun is just setting out on the path of advancement — how could one deceive one's lord?"
translations.idiomatic: Some urged Kou Zhun to inflate his age. He replied, "I am just beginning my career — how could I deceive the Emperor?"

sentences.zh: 後中第，授大理評事，知歸州巴東、大名府成安縣。

translations.literal: Later he passed the examination and was appointed case reviewer of the Court of Judicial Review, and put in charge of Badong in Guizhou and Cheng'an County in Daming Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Later he passed the examination. He was appointed case reviewer of the Court of Judicial Review and put in charge of Badong in Guizhou and Cheng'an County in Daming Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 每期會賦役，未嘗輒出符移，唯具鄉里姓名揭縣門，百姓莫敢後期。

translations.literal: Each time taxes and corvée labor came due, he never casually issued official summons. He merely posted the names and places of residence at the county gate, and the people dared not be late.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever taxes and corvée labor came due, he never casually issued official summons. He merely posted residents' names and hamlets at the county gate, and no one dared miss the deadline.

sentences.zh: 累遷殿中丞、通判鄆州。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to palace attendant and serving as administrative assistant at Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive appointments to palace attendant and administrative assistant at Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 召試學士院，授右正言、直史館，為三司度支推官，轉鹽鐵判官。

translations.literal: Summoned for examination at the Hanlin Academy, he was appointed Right Remonstrance Grandee and compiler in the Historiography Institute, served as investigating officer of the Revenue Bureau of the Three Commissions, and then transferred to salt and iron commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned for examination at the Hanlin Academy, he received appointment as Right Remonstrance Grandee and compiler in the Historiography Institute, served as investigating officer of the Revenue Bureau of the Three Commissions, and was then transferred to salt and iron commissioner.

sentences.zh: 會詔百官言事，而準極陳利害，帝益器重之。

translations.literal: When an edict summoned all officials to speak on affairs, Zhun set forth the advantages and disadvantages at length, and the Emperor came to esteem him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: When an edict called on all officials to speak on affairs of state, Kou Zhun laid out the pros and cons at length, and the Emperor came to esteem him all the more.

sentences.zh: 擢尚書虞部郎中、樞密院直學士，判吏部東銓。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Gentleman of the Department of Parks and Forests in the Ministry of Works, Hanlin Academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs, and put in charge of the eastern selection board of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Gentleman of the Department of Parks and Forests in the Ministry of Works and Hanlin Academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs, and put in charge of the eastern selection board of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 嘗奏事殿中，語不合，帝怒起，準輒引帝衣，令帝復坐，事決乃退。

translations.literal: Once when reporting in the hall, their words did not agree. The Emperor rose in anger. Zhun at once took hold of the Emperor's robe, made the Emperor sit again, and only withdrew after the matter was decided.
translations.idiomatic: Once, while reporting in the hall, their words failed to agree. The Emperor rose in anger. Kou Zhun immediately seized the Emperor's robe and made him sit again; he withdrew only after the matter was settled.

sentences.zh: 上由是嘉之，曰：「朕得寇準，猶文皇之得魏徵也。」

translations.literal: The Emperor thereupon praised him, saying: "In gaining Kou Zhun, I am like Emperor Wen in gaining Wei Zheng."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor thereupon praised him, saying, "In gaining Kou Zhun, I am like Emperor Taizong of Tang in gaining Wei Zheng."

sentences.zh: 淳化二年春，大旱，太宗延近臣問時政得失，眾以天數對。

translations.literal: In the spring of the second year of Chunhua there was great drought. Taizong invited close ministers to discuss the gains and losses of current policy. The multitude answered in terms of Heaven's decree.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the second year of Chunhua, a severe drought struck. Emperor Taizong summoned his close ministers to discuss what was right and wrong in current governance. Most answered in terms of Heaven's will.

sentences.zh: 準對曰：「《洪範》天人之際，應若影響，大旱之證，蓋刑有所不平也。」

translations.literal: Zhun answered: "The Hong Fan treats the nexus between Heaven and man as responding like shadow to form. The sign of great drought — surely punishments are in some respect unjust."
translations.idiomatic: Kou Zhun answered, "The Hong Fan treats the bond between Heaven and man as responding like shadow to form. This great drought is a sign that punishments have been unjust."

sentences.zh: 太宗怒，起入禁中。

translations.literal: Taizong grew angry, rose, and entered the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong grew angry, rose, and withdrew into the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 頃之，召準問所以不平狀，準曰：「願召二府至，臣即言之。」

translations.literal: Before long he summoned Zhun and asked the particulars of the injustice. Zhun said: "I wish the two bureaus to be summoned — then your servant will speak."
translations.idiomatic: Before long he summoned Kou Zhun and asked for particulars of the injustice. Kou Zhun said, "Summon the two bureaus, and I will speak."

sentences.zh: 有詔召二府入，準乃言曰：「頃者祖吉、王淮皆侮法受賕，吉贓少乃伏誅；

translations.literal: There was an edict summoning the two bureaus to enter. Zhun then spoke: "Recently Zu Ji and Wang Huai both defied the law and took bribes. Ji, whose illicit gains were small, was put to death;
translations.idiomatic: An edict summoned the two bureaus. Kou Zhun then said, "Recently Zu Ji and Wang Huai both flouted the law and accepted bribes. Ji, whose illicit gains were comparatively small, was executed;

sentences.zh: 淮以參政沔之弟，盜主守財至千萬，止杖，仍復其官，非不平而何？」

translations.literal: Huai, as younger brother of Participating Grand Counselor Mian, stole and embezzled funds under his custody to the amount of ten million, yet received only beating with the rod and was still restored to office — what is this if not injustice?"
translations.idiomatic: Huai, as younger brother of Participating Grand Counselor Li Mian, embezzled funds under his custody to the tune of ten million, yet received only a beating with the rod and was restored to office — what is this if not injustice?"

sentences.zh: 太宗以問沔，沔頓首謝，於是切責沔，而知準為可用矣。

translations.literal: Taizong questioned Mian on it. Mian bowed his head in apology. Thereupon he sharply rebuked Mian, and came to know that Zhun was employable.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong questioned Li Mian. Mian bowed his head and apologized. The Emperor then sharply rebuked him and came to recognize that Kou Zhun was a man he could use.

sentences.zh: 即拜準左諫議大夫、樞密副使，改同知院事。

translations.literal: He at once invested Zhun as Left Remonstrance Grandee and Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, changing his title to co-administrator of the bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately appointed Kou Zhun Left Remonstrance Grandee and Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, with the concurrent title co-administrator of the bureau.

sentences.zh: 準與知院張遜數爭事上前。

translations.literal: Zhun and Commissioner Zhang Xun often disputed matters before the Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Kou Zhun and the bureau commissioner Zhang Xun often argued before the Emperor.

sentences.zh: 他日，與溫仲舒偕行，道逢狂人迎馬呼萬歲，判左金吾王賓與遜雅相善，遜嗾上其事。

translations.literal: Another day, walking together with Wen Zhongshu, on the road they met a madman who came forward to the horse crying "Long live the Emperor!" Left Commandant of Golden Guards Wang Bin was on cordial terms with Xun. Xun prompted the Emperor regarding the matter.
translations.idiomatic: One day, walking with Wen Zhongshu, they met a madman who ran up to their horses crying "Long live the Emperor!" Left Commandant of Golden Guards Wang Bin was close to Zhang Xun, and Xun prompted the Emperor regarding the incident.

sentences.zh: 準引仲舒為證，遜令賓獨奏，其辭頗厲，且互斥其短。

translations.literal: Zhun cited Zhongshu as witness. Xun had Bin report alone. The words were quite severe, and they mutually exposed one another's faults.
translations.idiomatic: Kou Zhun cited Zhongshu as witness. Xun had Bin report alone. The language was harsh, and they mutually exposed one another's faults.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，謫遜，準亦罷知青州。

translations.literal: The Emperor grew angry, demoted Xun, and also dismissed Zhun from his post as prefect of Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor grew angry, demoted Zhang Xun, and also dismissed Kou Zhun from his post as prefect of Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 帝顧準厚，既行，念之，常不樂。

translations.literal: The Emperor regarded Zhun with deep favor. After he had gone, the Emperor missed him and was often displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong had deep affection for Kou Zhun. After Kou Zhun left, he missed him and was often melancholy.

sentences.zh: 語左右曰：「寇準在青州樂乎？」

translations.literal: He said to those at his side: "Is Kou Zhun happy in Qingzhou?"
translations.idiomatic: He said to those around him, "Is Kou Zhun happy in Qingzhou?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「準得善藩，當不苦也」數日，輒復問。

translations.literal: They answered: "Zhun has been given a good fief — he probably suffers no hardship." Within days he asked again.
translations.idiomatic: They answered, "Kou Zhun has been given a pleasant prefecture — he is probably not suffering." Within days he asked again.

sentences.zh: 左右揣帝意且復召用準，因對曰：「陛下思準不少忘，聞準日縱酒，未知亦念陛下乎？」

translations.literal: Those at his side guessed that the Emperor intended to recall Zhun, and so answered: "Your Majesty thinks of Zhun and seldom forgets him. I hear Zhun indulges in wine daily — does he also think of Your Majesty, one wonders?"
translations.idiomatic: Those around him guessed the Emperor intended to recall Kou Zhun and answered, "Your Majesty thinks of Kou Zhun and seldom forgets him. I hear Kou Zhun drinks heavily every day — one wonders whether he also thinks of Your Majesty?"

sentences.zh: 帝默然。

translations.literal: The Emperor fell silent.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor fell silent.

sentences.zh: 明年，召拜參知政事。

translations.literal: The next year he was summoned and invested as Participant in Governance.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Kou Zhun was recalled and appointed Participant in Governance.

sentences.zh: 自唐末，蕃戶有居渭南者。

translations.literal: Since the end of Tang, foreign households had lived south of the Wei River.
translations.idiomatic: Since the end of the Tang, barbarian households had settled south of the Wei River.

sentences.zh: 溫仲舒知秦州，驅之渭北，立堡柵以限其往來。

translations.literal: Wen Zhongshu, as prefect of Qinzhou, drove them north of the Wei and established stockades to restrict their comings and goings.
translations.idiomatic: When Wen Zhongshu served as prefect of Qinzhou, he drove them north of the Wei and built stockades to restrict their movements.

sentences.zh: 太宗覽奏不懌，曰：「古羌戎尚雜處伊、洛，彼蕃夷易動難安，一有調發，將重困吾關中矣。」

translations.literal: Taizong perused the memorial with displeasure and said: "In antiquity the Qiang and Rong still mixed with the people on the Yi and Luo rivers. Those foreign tribes are easily stirred and hard to pacify. Once mobilization is ordered, it will severely burden our Guanzhong region."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong read the memorial with displeasure and said, "In antiquity the Qiang and Rong still lived among the people along the Yi and Luo. Those frontier tribes are easily stirred and hard to pacify. Once orders for mobilization go out, our Guanzhong region will be severely burdened."

sentences.zh: 準言：「唐宋璟不賞邊功，卒致開元太平。

translations.literal: Zhun said: "During the Tang, Song Jing did not reward frontier achievements, and in the end brought about the Taiping era of Kaiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Kou Zhun said, "Under the Tang, Song Jing refused to reward frontier achievements, and in the end helped bring about the peace of the Kaiyuan reign.

sentences.zh: 疆埸之臣邀功以稔禍，深可戒也。」

translations.literal: Frontier officials seeking achievement thereby accumulate disaster — this is deeply to be warned against."
translations.idiomatic: When frontier officials seek credit and thereby accumulate disaster, the lesson is grave indeed."

sentences.zh: 帝因命準使渭北，安撫族帳，而徙仲舒鳳翔。

translations.literal: The Emperor thereupon ordered Zhun to go to the north bank of the Wei to pacify the tribal households, and transferred Zhongshu to Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor thereupon sent Kou Zhun north of the Wei to pacify the tribal households and transferred Wen Zhongshu to Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 至道元年，加給事中。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhidao he was additionally given the title of Supervising Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhidao he was additionally appointed Supervising Secretary.

sentences.zh: 時太宗在位久，馮拯等上疏乞立儲貳，帝怒，斥之嶺南，中外無敢言者。

translations.literal: At the time Taizong had reigned long. Feng Zheng and others submitted a memorial begging that an heir apparent be established. The Emperor grew angry and banished them to Lingnan. Within and without the court none dared speak.
translations.idiomatic: By then Emperor Taizong had reigned a long while. Feng Zheng and others submitted a memorial requesting that a crown prince be named. The Emperor grew angry and banished them to Lingnan. No one inside or outside the court dared speak further.

sentences.zh: 準初自青州召還，入見，帝足創甚，自褰衣以示準，且曰：「卿來何緩耶？」

translations.literal: When Zhun was first recalled from Qingzhou and entered for audience, the Emperor's foot wound was severe. He himself lifted his garment to show Zhun, and said: "Why have you come so slowly?"
translations.idiomatic: When Kou Zhun was first recalled from Qingzhou and granted an audience, the Emperor's foot wound was severe. He lifted his own robe to show Kou Zhun and said, "Why did you take so long to come?"

sentences.zh: 準對曰：「臣非召不得至京師。」

translations.literal: Zhun answered: "Your servant cannot reach the capital unless summoned."
translations.idiomatic: Kou Zhun answered, "I could not reach the capital unless summoned."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「朕諸子孰可以付神器者？」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Which of my sons may be entrusted with the sacred vessel?"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "Which of my sons can be entrusted with the imperial succession?"

sentences.zh: 準曰：「陛下為天下擇君，謀及婦人、中官，不可也；

translations.literal: Zhun said: "Your Majesty selects a lord for the realm — to consult women or eunuchs is not permitted;
translations.idiomatic: Kou Zhun said, "Your Majesty is choosing a ruler for the realm. You must not consult women or eunuchs;

sentences.zh: 謀及近臣，不可也；

translations.literal: to consult close ministers is not permitted;
translations.idiomatic: you must not consult close ministers, either;

sentences.zh: 唯陛下擇所以副天下望者。」

translations.literal: only Your Majesty may choose one who fulfills the hopes of the realm."
translations.idiomatic: only Your Majesty should choose one who fulfills the hopes of the realm."

sentences.zh: 帝俯首久之，屏左右曰：「襄王可乎？」

translations.literal: The Emperor bowed his head a long while, dismissed those at his side, and said: "Would the Prince of Xiang do?"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor bowed his head a long while, dismissed those around him, and said, "Would the Prince of Xiang do?"

sentences.zh: 準曰：「知子莫若父，聖慮既以為可，願即決定。」

translations.literal: Zhun said: "No one knows a son like his father. Since Your Sage's thought already deems him suitable, I wish you would decide at once."
translations.idiomatic: Kou Zhun said, "No one knows a son like his father. Since Your Majesty already deems him suitable, please decide at once."

sentences.zh: 帝遂以襄王為開封尹，改封壽王，於是立為皇太子。

translations.literal: The Emperor thereupon made the Prince of Xiang Commissioner of Kaifeng, changed his title to Prince of Shou, and thus established him as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor thereupon made the Prince of Xiang Commissioner of Kaifeng, renamed him Prince of Shou, and established him as crown prince.

sentences.zh: 廟見還，京師之人擁道喜躍，曰：「少年天子也。」

translations.literal: After the temple audience and his return, the people of the capital thronged the road in joy, saying: "A young Son of Heaven!"
translations.idiomatic: After the temple audience and his return, the people of the capital thronged the road in delight, crying, "A young Son of Heaven!"

sentences.zh: 帝聞之不懌，召準謂曰：「人心遽屬太子，欲置我何地？」

translations.literal: The Emperor heard this with displeasure, summoned Zhun, and said: "The people's hearts suddenly turn to the crown prince — where does this leave me?"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor heard this with displeasure, summoned Kou Zhun, and said, "The people's hearts have suddenly turned to the crown prince — where does that leave me?"

sentences.zh: 準再拜賀曰：「此社稷之福也。」

translations.literal: Zhun bowed twice in congratulations and said: "This is a blessing for the altars of state."
translations.idiomatic: Kou Zhun bowed twice in congratulations and said, "This is a blessing for the altars of state."

sentences.zh: 帝入語後嬪，宮中皆前賀。

translations.literal: The Emperor entered and spoke to the palace ladies. Throughout the inner palace all came forward to congratulate.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor went inside to tell the consorts, and throughout the palace all came forward to congratulate.

sentences.zh: 復出，延準飲，極醉而罷。

translations.literal: He came out again, invited Zhun to drink, and only dismissed him when utterly drunk.
translations.idiomatic: He came out again, invited Kou Zhun to drink, and sent him away only when he was thoroughly drunk.

sentences.zh: 二年，祠南郊，中外官皆進秩。

translations.literal: In the second year, when sacrifices were made at the Southern Suburb, officials within and without the court all received promotion in rank.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, when sacrifices were offered at the Southern Suburb, officials throughout the government all received promotions in rank.

sentences.zh: 準素所喜者多得臺省清要官，所惡不及知者退序進之。

translations.literal: Those Zhun had always favored mostly obtained coveted posts in the censorate and secretariat. Those he disliked, though they had not yet been notified, were pushed back in the promotion queue.
translations.idiomatic: Those Kou Zhun favored mostly received coveted posts in the censorate and secretariat. Those he disliked, before they even knew it, were pushed back in the promotion queue.

sentences.zh: 彭惟節位素居馮拯下，拯轉虞部員外郎，惟節轉屯田員外郎，章奏列銜，惟節猶處其下。

translations.literal: Peng Weijie's rank had always been below Feng Zheng's. Zheng was transferred to Assistant Director of the Department of Parks and Forests; Weijie was transferred to Assistant Director of the Department of Public Works. In memorials their names were listed in order, yet Weijie still ranked below.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Weijie's rank had always been below Feng Zheng's. Zheng was promoted to Assistant Director of the Department of Parks and Forests and Weijie to Assistant Director of the Department of Public Works, but when their names appeared together on memorials, Weijie still ranked below.

sentences.zh: 準怒，堂帖戒拯毋亂朝制。

translations.literal: Zhun grew angry and issued an office notice warning Zheng not to disrupt court regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Kou Zhun grew angry and issued an office notice warning Feng Zheng not to flout court regulations.

sentences.zh: 拯憤極，陳準擅權，又條上嶺南官吏除拜不平數事。

translations.literal: Zheng was furious to the utmost. He reported that Zhun had arrogated authority, and also itemized several instances of unjust appointments among Lingnan officials.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Zheng was furious. He accused Kou Zhun of arrogating authority and itemized several cases of unjust appointments among Lingnan officials.

sentences.zh: 廣東轉運使康戩亦言：呂端、張洎、李昌齡皆準所引，端德之，洎能曲奉準，而昌齡畏愞，不敢與準抗，故得以任胸臆，亂經制。

translations.literal: Guangdong Transport Commissioner Kang Zhan also said: Lu Duan, Zhang Zhi, and Li Changling were all introduced by Zhun. Duan values his virtue; Zhi can bow and scrape to please Zhun; and Changling is timid and fearful, not daring to oppose Zhun — thus Zhun can indulge his whims and disrupt established regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Guangdong Transport Commissioner Kang Zhan also said that Lu Duan, Zhang Zhi, and Li Changling had all been promoted by Kou Zhun. Duan admired his integrity, Zhi could flatter him, and Changling was timid and dared not oppose him — so Kou Zhun indulged his whims and disrupted established regulations.

sentences.zh: 太宗怒，準適祀太廟攝事，召責端等。

translations.literal: The Emperor grew angry. Zhun happened to be officiating at the sacrifice at the Imperial Ancestral Temple. He summoned and rebuked Duan and the others.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong grew angry. Kou Zhun happened to be officiating at sacrifices at the Imperial Ancestral Temple. The Emperor summoned Lu Duan and the others and rebuked them.

sentences.zh: 端曰：「準性剛自任，臣等不欲數爭，慮傷國體。」

translations.literal: Duan said: "Zhun by nature is hard and self-willed. We did not wish to dispute repeatedly, fearing harm to the dignity of state."
translations.idiomatic: Lu Duan said, "Kou Zhun is by nature rigid and self-willed. We did not wish to argue with him repeatedly, fearing harm to the dignity of state."

sentences.zh: 因再拜請罪。

translations.literal: He thereupon bowed twice in request of pardon.
translations.idiomatic: He bowed twice and asked forgiveness.

sentences.zh: 及準入對，帝語及馮拯事，自辯。

translations.literal: When Zhun entered for audience, the Emperor spoke of the Feng Zheng affair, and Zhun defended himself.
translations.idiomatic: When Kou Zhun entered for audience, the Emperor brought up the Feng Zheng affair, and Kou Zhun defended himself.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「若廷辯，失執政體。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "If there is open debate in court, it loses the dignity befitting the governing administration."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "Open debate in court undermines the dignity of the governing administration."

sentences.zh: 準猶力爭不已，又持中書簿論曲直於帝前，帝益不悅，因歎曰：「鼠雀尚知人意，況人乎？」

translations.literal: Zhun still strove in argument without cease, and furthermore took the Secretariat register to argue right and wrong before the Emperor. The Emperor grew all the more displeased and sighed: "Even mice and sparrows know men's hearts — how much more men?"
translations.idiomatic: Kou Zhun still argued fiercely, and even brought the Secretariat register before the Emperor to argue right and wrong. The Emperor grew all the more displeased and sighed, "Even mice and sparrows know what people want — how much more so men?"

sentences.zh: 遂罷準知鄧州。

translations.literal: He thereupon dismissed Zhun from his post as prefect of Dengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He then dismissed Kou Zhun from his post as prefect of Dengzhou.

sentences.zh: 真宗即位，遷尚書工部侍郎。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhenzong ascended the throne, Zhun was transferred to Vice Minister of the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhenzong ascended the throne, Kou Zhun was transferred to Vice Minister of the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 咸平初，徙河陽，改同州。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xianping he was transferred to Heyang and then changed to Tongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Xianping he was transferred to Heyang and then reassigned to Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 三年，朝京師，行次閿鄉，又徙鳳翔府。

translations.literal: In the third year, while proceeding to court at the capital, when he reached Wenxiang he was again transferred to Fengxiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, while traveling to the capital for court, he was transferred again to Fengxiang Prefecture when he reached Wenxiang.

sentences.zh: 帝幸大名，詔赴行在所，遷刑部，權知開封府。

translations.literal: The Emperor visited Daming. An edict ordered him to proceed to the temporary palace. He was transferred to the Ministry of Justice and given provisional charge of Kaifeng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor visited Daming, an edict ordered Kou Zhun to his temporary residence. He was transferred to the Ministry of Justice and given provisional charge of Kaifeng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 六年，遷兵部，為三司使。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was transferred to the Ministry of War and made commissioner of the Three Commissions.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was transferred to the Ministry of War and made commissioner of the Three Commissions.

sentences.zh: 時合鹽鐵、度支、戶部為一使，真宗命準裁定，遂以六判官分掌之，繁簡始適中。

translations.literal: At the time the salt and iron, revenue, and household bureaus were combined into one commissioner. Zhenzong ordered Zhun to determine the arrangement. Thereupon six commissioners were appointed to divide supervision among them, and complexity and simplicity came to be properly balanced.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the salt and iron, revenue, and household bureaus were combined into one commission. Emperor Zhenzong ordered Kou Zhun to determine the arrangement. He divided oversight among six deputy commissioners, and the workload was finally brought into balance.

sentences.zh: 帝久欲相準，患其剛直難獨任。

translations.literal: The Emperor had long wished to make Zhun chief minister, but feared that his rigidity and uprightness made him hard to employ alone.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor had long wished to make Kou Zhun chief minister, but feared his rigidity and uprightness made him difficult to employ on his own.

sentences.zh: 景德元年，以畢士安參知政事，逾月，並命同中書門下平章事，準以集賢殿大學士位士安下。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingde, Bi Shi'an was appointed Participant in Governance. After more than a month, both were together appointed Grand Counselors of State. Zhun, as Hanlin Academician of the Hall for Cherishing Worthies, ranked below Shi'an.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jingde, Bi Shi'an was appointed Participant in Governance. More than a month later both were appointed Grand Counselors of State. Kou Zhun, as Hanlin Academician of the Hall for Cherishing Worthies, ranked below Bi Shi'an.

sentences.zh: 是時，契丹內寇，縱游騎掠深、祁間，小不利輒引去，徜徉無鬥意。

translations.literal: At this time the Khitans raided inward. They sent roaming cavalry to plunder between Shen and Qi. At the slightest setback they withdrew, roaming at leisure with no intent to fight.
translations.idiomatic: At this time the Khitans raided deep into Song territory. Their roaming cavalry plundered between Shenzhou and Qizhou. At the slightest setback they withdrew and wandered at leisure, showing no desire to fight.

sentences.zh: 準曰：「是狃我也。

translations.literal: Zhun said: "This is to make us complacent.
translations.idiomatic: Kou Zhun said, "They are trying to make us complacent.

sentences.zh: 請練師命將，簡驍銳據要害以備之。」

translations.literal: I request that troops be drilled and generals appointed, and picked elite forces posted at strategic points to prepare against them."
translations.idiomatic: Train the troops, appoint generals, and post picked elite forces at strategic points to guard against them."

sentences.zh: 是冬，契丹果大入。

translations.literal: That winter the Khitans indeed invaded in force.
translations.idiomatic: That winter the Khitans indeed invaded in force.

sentences.zh: 急書一夕凡五至，準不發，飲笑自如。

translations.literal: Urgent dispatches arrived five times in one night. Zhun did not open them but drank and laughed as usual.
translations.idiomatic: Urgent dispatches arrived five times in one night. Kou Zhun did not open them but drank and laughed as usual.

sentences.zh: 明日，同列以聞，帝大駭，以問準。

translations.literal: The next day his colleagues reported this. The Emperor was greatly alarmed and questioned Zhun.
translations.idiomatic: The next day his colleagues reported this to the Emperor. The Emperor was greatly alarmed and questioned Kou Zhun.

sentences.zh: 準曰：「陛下欲了此，不過五日爾。」

translations.literal: Zhun said: "If Your Majesty wishes to settle this, it will take no more than five days."
translations.idiomatic: Kou Zhun said, "If Your Majesty wishes to settle this affair, it will take no more than five days."

sentences.zh: 因請帝幸澶州。

translations.literal: He then requested that the Emperor proceed to Chuanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He then asked the Emperor to proceed to Chuanzhou.

sentences.zh: 同列懼，欲退，準止之，令候駕起。

translations.literal: His colleagues were afraid and wished to withdraw. Zhun stopped them and ordered them to wait until the imperial procession set out.
translations.idiomatic: His colleagues were frightened and wished to withdraw. Kou Zhun stopped them and ordered them to wait until the imperial procession set out.

sentences.zh: 帝難之，欲還內，準曰：「陛下入則臣不得見，大事去矣，請毋還而行。」

translations.literal: The Emperor found it difficult and wished to return inside. Zhun said: "If Your Majesty enters, your servant cannot see you — the great affair is lost. I beg you not to return but to proceed."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor hesitated and wanted to go back inside. Kou Zhun said, "If Your Majesty withdraws, I will not be able to see you and the great affair will be lost. Please do not go back — proceed at once."

sentences.zh: 帝乃議親征，召群臣問方略。

translations.literal: The Emperor then deliberated on a personal campaign and summoned the grand assembly to ask strategy.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor then deliberated on leading the campaign in person and summoned the grand assembly to ask their counsel.

sentences.zh: 既而契丹圍瀛州，直犯貝、魏，中外震駭。

translations.literal: Before long the Khitans besieged Yingzhou and struck straight at Bei and Wei. Within and without the court all were shaken with terror.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the Khitans besieged Yingzhou and drove straight at Bei and Wei. Court and country alike were shaken with terror.

sentences.zh: 參知政事王欽若，江南人也，請幸金陵。

translations.literal: Participating Grand Counselor Wang Qinruo, a man of Jiangnan, requested that the Emperor proceed to Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: Participating Grand Counselor Wang Qinruo, a native of Jiangnan, urged the Emperor to proceed to Jinling.

sentences.zh: 陳堯叟，蜀人也，請幸成都。

translations.literal: Chen Yaosou, a man of Shu, requested that the Emperor proceed to Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yaosou, a native of Shu, urged the Emperor to proceed to Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 帝問準，準心知二人謀，乃陽若不知，曰：「誰為陛下畫此策者，罪可誅也。

translations.literal: The Emperor asked Zhun. Zhun knew in his heart it was the two men's plan, yet feigned ignorance and said: "Whoever devised this strategy for Your Majesty — his crime deserves death.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor asked Kou Zhun. Kou Zhun knew the two men were behind the proposal, but feigned ignorance and said, "Whoever devised this strategy for Your Majesty deserves death.

sentences.zh: 今陛下神武，將臣協和，若大駕親征，賊自當遁去。

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty is divinely martial, and generals and ministers are in harmony. If the imperial carriage campaigns in person, the enemy will of themselves flee.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty is divinely martial, and generals and ministers are in harmony. If you lead the campaign in person, the enemy will flee of their own accord.

sentences.zh: 不然，出奇以撓其謀，堅守以老其師，勞佚之勢，我得勝算矣。

translations.literal: If not, strike with unexpected moves to thwart their designs; hold firmly to wear down their troops. In the balance of fatigue and rest, we hold the winning calculation.
translations.idiomatic: If not, strike with unexpected moves to thwart their designs and hold firm to wear down their troops. With fatigue and rest weighing in our favor, victory is assured.

sentences.zh: 奈何棄廟社欲幸楚、蜀遠地，所在人心崩潰，賊乘勢深入，天下可復保邪？」

translations.literal: How could one abandon the altars of state and wish to proceed to distant Chu and Shu? Wherever one goes, hearts will collapse; the enemy will ride the momentum and strike deep — how could the realm ever be preserved?"
translations.idiomatic: How can we abandon the altars of state and flee to distant Jinling or Chengdu? Hearts will collapse wherever you go, and the enemy will ride the momentum and strike deep — how can the realm be preserved?"

sentences.zh: 遂請帝幸澶州。

translations.literal: He then requested that the Emperor proceed to Chuanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He then asked the Emperor to proceed to Chuanzhou.

sentences.zh: 及至南城，契丹兵方盛，眾請駐蹕以覘軍勢。

translations.literal: When they reached the southern city, Khitan troops were at their peak strength. The multitude requested halting the imperial progress to observe the military situation.
translations.idiomatic: When they reached the southern city, Khitan forces were at full strength. Many urged halting the imperial progress to assess the military situation.

sentences.zh: 準固請曰：「陛下不過河，則人心益危，敵氣未懾，非所以取威決勝也。

translations.literal: Zhun firmly requested: "If Your Majesty does not cross the river, hearts will grow more fearful and the enemy's spirit will not be cowed — this is not the way to display might and decide victory.
translations.idiomatic: Kou Zhun pressed firmly: "If Your Majesty does not cross the river, hearts will grow more fearful and the enemy will not be cowed — this is not how to display imperial might and decide the battle.

sentences.zh: 且王超領勁兵屯中山以扼其亢，李繼隆、石保吉分大陣以扼其左右肘，四方征鎮赴援者日至，何疑而不進？」

translations.literal: Moreover, Wang Chao leads elite troops stationed at Zhongshan to check their throat; Li Jilong and Shi Baoji divide great formations to check their left and right arms. Reinforcements from the expeditionary commands arrive daily from all quarters — why hesitate and not advance?"
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Wang Chao holds elite troops at Zhongshan to check their throat; Li Jilong and Shi Baoji deploy great formations to check their flanks. Reinforcements from expeditionary commands arrive daily from all quarters — why hesitate to advance?"

sentences.zh: 眾議畢懼，準力爭之，不決。

translations.literal: All deliberation ended in fear. Zhun strove in argument, yet no decision was reached.
translations.idiomatic: Deliberation ended in fear. Kou Zhun argued fiercely, but no decision was reached.

sentences.zh: 出遇高瓊於屏間，謂曰：「太尉受國恩，今日有以報乎？」

translations.literal: Going out he met Gao Qiong between screens and said: "Grand Commandant, you have received the state's grace — have you something with which to repay it today?"
translations.idiomatic: On his way out he met Gao Qiong between the screens and said, "Grand Commandant, you have received the state's favor — can you repay it today?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「瓊武人，願效死。」

translations.literal: He answered: "Qiong is a military man — I wish to give my life in service."
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "I am a military man — I am ready to die in your service."

sentences.zh: 準復入對，瓊隨立庭下，準厲聲曰：「陛下不以臣言為然，盍試問瓊等？」

translations.literal: Zhun entered again for audience. Qiong followed and stood beneath the hall court. Zhun said in a stern voice: "If Your Majesty does not deem your servant's words correct, why not try asking Qiong and the others?"
translations.idiomatic: Kou Zhun re-entered for audience. Gao Qiong followed and stood in the courtyard below. Kou Zhun said sternly, "If Your Majesty does not accept my counsel, why not ask Gao Qiong and the others?"

sentences.zh: 瓊即仰奏曰：「寇準言是。」

translations.literal: Qiong at once looked up and reported: "Kou Zhun's words are correct."
translations.idiomatic: Gao Qiong looked up and reported, "Kou Zhun is right."

sentences.zh: 準曰：「機不可失，宜趣駕。」

translations.literal: Zhun said: "The moment cannot be lost — the imperial carriage should be urged forward."
translations.idiomatic: Kou Zhun said, "The moment must not be lost — urge the imperial carriage forward."

sentences.zh: 瓊即麾衛士進輦，帝遂渡河，御北城門樓，遠近望見御蓋，踴躍歡呼，聲聞數十里。

translations.literal: Qiong at once waved the imperial guards to advance the carriage. The Emperor thereupon crossed the river, mounted the gate tower of the northern wall, and from far and near all who saw the imperial canopy leaped and shouted in joy; the sound was heard for several tens of li.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Qiong waved the imperial guards to advance the carriage. The Emperor crossed the river and mounted the northern gate tower. From far and near all who saw the imperial canopy leaped and shouted for joy; their cries carried for dozens of li.

sentences.zh: 契丹相視驚愕，不能成列。

translations.literal: The Khitan looked at one another in shock and alarm, unable to form ranks.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan stared at one another in shock, unable to hold their formation.

sentences.zh: 帝盡以軍事委準，準承制專決，號令明肅，士卒喜悅。

translations.literal: The Emperor entirely entrusted military affairs to Zhun. Zhun received imperial orders and decided alone; commands were clear and stern, and soldiers rejoiced.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor entrusted all military affairs to Kou Zhun, who exercised sole authority under imperial commission. His orders were clear and strict, and the soldiers were pleased.

sentences.zh: 敵數千騎乘勝薄城下，詔士卒迎擊，斬獲大半，乃引去。

translations.literal: Several thousand enemy horsemen, riding victory, pressed close beneath the city. He ordered soldiers to meet and strike; more than half were killed or captured, and they then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Several thousand enemy horsemen pressed the walls in pursuit of victory. He ordered troops to sally forth; more than half were killed or captured, and the rest withdrew.

sentences.zh: 上還行宮，留準居城上，徐使人視準何為。

translations.literal: The Emperor returned to the traveling palace, leaving Zhun dwelling on the wall, and gradually sent someone to observe what Zhun was doing.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor returned to the traveling palace and left Kou Zhun on the wall, then gradually sent someone to see what he was doing.

sentences.zh: 準方與楊億飲博，歌謔歡呼。

translations.literal: Zhun was just then drinking and gambling with Yang Yi, singing, jesting, and shouting in joy.
translations.idiomatic: Kou Zhun was drinking and gambling with Yang Yi, singing, jesting, and cheering.

sentences.zh: 帝喜曰：「準如此，吾復何憂？」

translations.literal: The Emperor said joyfully: "With Zhun like this, what further worry have I?"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said happily, "With Kou Zhun like this, what have I to worry about?"

sentences.zh: 相持十餘日，其統軍撻覽出督戰。

translations.literal: They faced each other for more than ten days. Their army commander Dalai came out to oversee the battle.
translations.idiomatic: The stalemate lasted more than ten days, until the Khitan commander Dalai came out to direct the fighting.

sentences.zh: 時威虎軍頭張瑰守床子弩，弩撼機發，矢中撻覽額，撻覽死，乃密奉書請盟。

translations.literal: At that time Weihu Corps head Zhang Gui manned the bed-mounted crossbow. The crossbow shook and the mechanism released; the arrow struck Dalai in the forehead. Dalai died, and they thereupon secretly presented a letter requesting alliance.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Gui, commander of the Weihu Corps, was operating a bed-mounted crossbow. When the weapon shook and released, the bolt struck Dalai in the forehead and killed him. The Khitan then secretly sent envoys requesting peace.

sentences.zh: 準不從，而使者來請益堅，帝將許之。

translations.literal: Zhun did not comply, but envoys came requesting with increasing firmness, and the Emperor was about to consent.
translations.idiomatic: Kou Zhun refused, but the envoys pressed their request ever more firmly, and the Emperor was about to agree.

sentences.zh: 準欲邀使稱臣，且獻幽州地。

translations.literal: Zhun wished to require the envoys to declare themselves subjects and also to present Youzhou territory.
translations.idiomatic: Kou Zhun wanted to require them to acknowledge vassalage and cede the Youzhou region.

sentences.zh: 帝厭兵，欲羈縻不絕而已。

translations.literal: The Emperor was weary of warfare and wished merely to keep them reined and attached without severing ties.
translations.idiomatic: Weary of war, the Emperor wanted only to keep them loosely bound without breaking ties.

sentences.zh: 有譖準幸兵以自取重者，準不得已，許之。

translations.literal: Someone slandered Zhun, saying he relied on the army to seek heavy weight for himself. Zhun had no choice and consented.
translations.idiomatic: Someone accused Kou Zhun of exploiting the military crisis to aggrandize himself, and Kou Zhun, having no choice, consented.

sentences.zh: 帝遣曹利用如軍中議歲幣，曰：「百萬以下皆可許也。」

translations.literal: The Emperor dispatched Cao Liyong to the army to negotiate annual tribute, saying: "Anything below one million may be granted."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor sent Cao Liyong to the army to negotiate the annual tribute, saying, "You may agree to anything below one million."
