sentences.zh: 準召利用至幄，語曰：「雖有敕，汝所許毋過三十萬，過三十萬，吾斬汝矣。」

translations.literal: Zhun summoned Liyong to the tent and said: "Although there is an edict, what you agree to must not exceed three hundred thousand. If it exceeds three hundred thousand, I will behead you."
translations.idiomatic: Kou Zhun summoned Cao Liyong to his tent and said, "Despite the edict, you must agree to no more than three hundred thousand. If you promise more, I will have your head."

sentences.zh: 利用至軍，果以三十萬成約而還。

translations.literal: Liyong reached the army and indeed concluded the agreement at three hundred thousand and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Liyong reached the enemy camp, concluded the pact at three hundred thousand, and returned.

sentences.zh: 河北罷兵，準之力也。

translations.literal: The cessation of warfare in Hebei was Zhun's power.
translations.idiomatic: The end of fighting in Hebei was Kou Zhun's doing.

sentences.zh: 準在相位，用人不以次，同列頗不悅。

translations.literal: Zhun, in the chancellor's position, employed men not according to order; colleagues were quite displeased.
translations.idiomatic: As chancellor, Kou Zhun appointed men out of turn, to the considerable displeasure of his colleagues.

sentences.zh: 它日，又除官，同列因吏持例簿以進。

translations.literal: Another day, when appointing officials again, colleagues had a clerk hold the precedent register and present it.
translations.idiomatic: On another occasion, when making appointments, his colleagues had a clerk bring forward the roster of precedents.

sentences.zh: 準曰：「宰相所以進賢退不肖也，若用例，一吏職爾。」

translations.literal: Zhun said: "The chancellor is for advancing the worthy and retiring the unworthy. If one uses precedents, that is only a clerk's duty."
translations.idiomatic: Kou Zhun said, "A chancellor exists to advance the worthy and remove the unworthy. If one need only follow precedent, that is a clerk's job."

sentences.zh: 二年，加中書侍郎兼工部尚書。

translations.literal: In the second year he was additionally appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat and concurrently Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of his tenure he was made Vice Director of the Secretariat and concurrently Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 準頗自矜澶淵之功，雖帝亦以此待準甚厚。

translations.literal: Zhun rather prided himself on his Chanyuan achievement, and even the Emperor on this account treated Zhun very generously.
translations.idiomatic: Kou Zhun rather prided himself on his success at Chanyuan, and even the Emperor treated him very generously on that account.

sentences.zh: 王欽若深嫉之。

translations.literal: Wang Qinruo deeply envied him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Qinruo deeply resented him.

sentences.zh: 一日會朝，準先退，帝目送之，欽若因進曰：「陛下敬寇準，為其有社稷功邪？」

translations.literal: One day at court assembly, Zhun withdrew first; the Emperor's eyes followed him as he departed. Qinruo thereupon advanced and said: "Your Majesty respects Kou Zhun — is it because he has service to the state and altars?"
translations.idiomatic: One day at court, Kou Zhun withdrew first while the Emperor watched him go. Wang Qinruo stepped forward and said, "Your Majesty holds Kou Zhun in high regard — is it because he has rendered great service to the realm?"

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「然。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "It is so."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "It is."

sentences.zh: 欽若曰：「澶淵之役，陛下不以為恥，而謂準有社稷功，何也？」

translations.literal: Qinruo said: "In the Chanyuan campaign, Your Majesty does not consider it shameful, yet you say Zhun has service to the state and altars — why?"
translations.idiomatic: Wang Qinruo said, "At Chanyuan, Your Majesty does not consider it shameful, yet you call Kou Zhun a savior of the realm — why?"

sentences.zh: 帝愕然曰：「何故？」

translations.literal: The Emperor said startled: "For what reason?"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor asked, startled, "Why do you say that?"

sentences.zh: 欽若曰：「城下之盟，《春秋》恥之。

translations.literal: Qinruo said: "A covenant beneath the walls — the Spring and Autumn Annals regard it as shameful.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Qinruo said, "A treaty sworn beneath the walls is a disgrace in the Spring and Autumn Annals.

sentences.zh: 澶淵之舉，是城下之盟也。

translations.literal: The Chanyuan undertaking was a covenant beneath the walls.
translations.idiomatic: What happened at Chanyuan was exactly such a treaty beneath the walls.

sentences.zh: 以萬乘之貴而為城下之盟，其何恥如之！」

translations.literal: For one of ten thousand chariots in honor to make a covenant beneath the walls — what shame could be like this!"
translations.idiomatic: For the sovereign of ten thousand chariots to swear a treaty beneath the walls — what could be more shameful!"

sentences.zh: 帝愀然為之不悅。

translations.literal: The Emperor's countenance fell and on account of this he was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor's face darkened and he was deeply displeased.

sentences.zh: 欽若曰：「陛下聞博乎？

translations.literal: Qinruo said: "Has Your Majesty heard of gambling?
translations.idiomatic: Wang Qinruo said, "Your Majesty, have you heard of gambling?

sentences.zh: 博者輸錢欲盡，乃罄所有出之，謂之孤注。

translations.literal: When gamblers have lost money and wish to exhaust it, they then exhaust all they possess and put it forth — this is called a lone wager.
translations.idiomatic: When gamblers, having lost heavily, wish to stake everything they have left, they pour it all out in one last bet — this is called staking everything on a single throw.

sentences.zh: 陛下，寇準之孤注也，斯亦危矣。」

translations.literal: Your Majesty, Kou Zhun is the lone wager — this too is perilous."
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty, you were Kou Zhun's lone wager — and that too was perilous."

sentences.zh: 由是帝顧準浸衰。

translations.literal: From this the Emperor's regard for Zhun gradually waned.
translations.idiomatic: From this the Emperor's favor toward Kou Zhun gradually waned.

sentences.zh: 明年，罷為刑部尚書、知陝州，遂用王旦為相。

translations.literal: The next year he was dismissed and made Minister of Justice and prefect of Shaanzhou; Wang Dan was thereupon employed as chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was removed as chancellor, appointed Minister of Justice and prefect of Shaanzhou, and Wang Dan was made chancellor in his place.

sentences.zh: 帝謂旦曰：「寇準多許人官，以為己恩。

translations.literal: The Emperor said to Dan: "Kou Zhun frequently grants men offices to make them his own grace.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor told Wang Dan, "Kou Zhun often hands out appointments to bind men to him in gratitude.

sentences.zh: 俟行，當深戒之。」

translations.literal: When he goes, you should deeply warn him of this."
translations.idiomatic: When he leaves, you must warn him firmly against this."

sentences.zh: 從封泰山，遷戶部尚書、知天雄軍。

translations.literal: Accompanying the feng at Mount Tai, he was transferred to Minister of Revenue and military commissioner of Tianxiong.
translations.idiomatic: He accompanied the feng sacrifice at Mount Tai and was transferred to Minister of Revenue and commissioner of the Tianxiong command.

sentences.zh: 祀汾陰，命提舉貝、德、博、洺、濱、棣巡檢捉賊公事，遷兵部尚書，入判都省。

translations.literal: At the sacrifice at Fenyin, he was ordered to oversee bandit-suppression affairs for Bei, De, Bo, Ming, Bin, and Di circuits; transferred to Minister of War; entered to judge the Central Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: During the Fenyin sacrifice he was charged with suppressing banditry in the Bei, De, Bo, Ming, Bin, and Di circuits, promoted to Minister of War, and recalled to the capital as director of the Central Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 幸亳州，權東京留守，為樞密院使、同平章事。

translations.literal: When the Emperor visited Bozhou, he acted as provisional Eastern Capital intendant, and was made commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs and Associate Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor visited Bozhou, Kou Zhun served as provisional Eastern Capital intendant and was made commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs and Associate Grand Councillor.

sentences.zh: 林特為三司使，以河北歲輸絹闕，督之甚急。

translations.literal: Lin Te served as commissioner of the Three Departments. Because the annual silk tribute from Hebei was deficient, he pressed it very urgently.
translations.idiomatic: Lin Te, commissioner of the Three Departments, pressed urgently for the annual silk tribute from Hebei, which was in arrears.

sentences.zh: 而準素惡特，頗助轉運使李士衡而沮特，且言在魏時嘗進河北絹五萬而三司不納，以至闕供，請劾主吏以下。

translations.literal: But Zhun had long hated Te and rather aided transport commissioner Li Shiheng while obstructing Te. He also said that while at Wei he had once presented fifty thousand bolts of Hebei silk but the Three Departments did not accept them, leading to deficient supply, and requested impeachment of the chief clerks downward.
translations.idiomatic: Kou Zhun had long disliked Lin Te and aided transport commissioner Li Shiheng while blocking Lin Te. He claimed that while stationed at Wei he had once sent fifty thousand bolts of Hebei silk that the Three Departments refused to accept, causing the shortfall, and asked that the responsible clerks be impeached.

sentences.zh: 然京師歲費絹百萬，準所助才五萬。

translations.literal: Yet the capital annually expended one million bolts of silk; what Zhun aided was only fifty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the capital's annual silk requirement was one million bolts — Kou Zhun's contribution was a mere fifty thousand.

sentences.zh: 帝不悅，謂王旦曰：「準剛忿如昔。」

translations.literal: The Emperor was displeased and said to Wang Dan: "Zhun is obstinate and resentful as before."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was displeased and told Wang Dan, "Kou Zhun is as stubborn and irascible as ever."

sentences.zh: 旦曰：「準好人懷惠，又欲人畏威，皆大臣所避。

translations.literal: Dan said: "Zhun likes men to harbor gratitude and also wants men to fear authority — both are things great ministers avoid.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dan said, "Kou Zhun likes men to feel obliged to him and also wants them to fear his wrath — both are traits a statesman should avoid.

sentences.zh: 而準乃為己任，此其短也。」

translations.literal: Yet Zhun took these as his own duties — this is his shortcoming."
translations.idiomatic: Yet Kou Zhun makes them his business — that is his flaw."

sentences.zh: 未幾，罷為武勝軍節度使、同平章事、判河南府，徙永興軍。

translations.literal: Before long he was dismissed and made military commissioner of Wusheng, Associate Grand Councillor, and judge of Henan Prefecture, transferred to Yongxing Command.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he was removed, made military commissioner of Wusheng and Associate Grand Councillor with jurisdiction over Henan Prefecture, then transferred to Yongxing Command.

sentences.zh: 天禧元年，改山南東道節度使，時巡檢朱能挾內侍都知周懷政詐為天書，上以問王旦。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianxi he was changed to military commissioner of Shannan East Circuit. At that time inspector Zhu Neng, relying on palace eunuch director Zhou Huaizheng, falsely made a Heavenly Scripture. The Emperor questioned Wang Dan about it.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tianxi he was transferred to military commissioner of Shannan East Circuit. At that time inspector Zhu Neng, with the palace eunuch director Zhou Huaizheng, forged a Heavenly Scripture. The Emperor consulted Wang Dan.

sentences.zh: 旦曰：「始不信天書者準也。

translations.literal: Dan said: "The one who from the first did not believe in Heavenly Scriptures was Zhun.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dan said, "Kou Zhun was the first to reject the Heavenly Scriptures.

sentences.zh: 今天書降，須令準上之。」

translations.literal: Now that a Heavenly Scripture has descended, he must be made to present it."
translations.idiomatic: Now that a Heavenly Scripture has appeared, Kou Zhun must be the one to present it."

sentences.zh: 準從上其書，中外皆以為非。

translations.literal: Zhun followed and presented the scripture; inside and outside all considered it wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Kou Zhun obeyed and presented the scripture, and opinion inside and outside the court held this unseemly.

sentences.zh: 遂拜中書侍郎兼吏部尚書、同平章事、景靈宮使。

translations.literal: He was thereupon appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat and concurrently Minister of Personnel, Associate Grand Councillor, and commissioner of the Jingling Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He was thereupon made Vice Director of the Secretariat and Minister of Personnel, Associate Grand Councillor, and commissioner of the Jingling Palace.

sentences.zh: 三年，祀南郊，進尚書右僕射、集賢殿大學士。

translations.literal: In the third year, at the southern suburb sacrifice, he was promoted to Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and Grand Academician of the Hall for Assembling Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, during the southern suburb sacrifice, he was promoted to Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and Grand Academician of the Hall for Assembling Worthies.

sentences.zh: 時真宗得風疾，劉太后預政於內，準請間曰：「皇太子人所屬望，願陛下思宗廟之重，傳以神器，擇方正大臣為羽翼。

translations.literal: At that time Zhenzong suffered wind ailment. Empress Dowager Liu participated in government within. Zhun requested private audience and said: "The Crown Prince is the one upon whom men's hopes rest. I wish Your Majesty would consider the weight of the ancestral temple, transmit the divine vessel, and select upright great ministers as wings.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhenzong was afflicted with wind disorder. Empress Dowager Liu was already involved in palace governance. Kou Zhun requested a private audience and said, "The Crown Prince enjoys the people's hopes. I urge Your Majesty to consider the weight of the ancestral temple, pass the imperial succession to him, and choose upright ministers to support him.

sentences.zh: 丁謂、錢惟演，佞人也，不可以輔少主。」

translations.literal: Ding Wei and Qian Weiyan are flatterers — they cannot assist a young lord."
translations.idiomatic: Ding Wei and Qian Weiyan are sycophants — they must not assist the young sovereign."

sentences.zh: 帝然之。

translations.literal: The Emperor approved this.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 準密令翰林學士楊億草表，請太子監國，且欲援億輔政。

translations.literal: Zhun secretly ordered Hanlin Academician Yang Yi to draft a memorial requesting the Crown Prince supervise the state, and also wished to enlist Yi to assist in governing.
translations.idiomatic: Kou Zhun secretly had Hanlin Academician Yang Yi draft a memorial asking that the Crown Prince supervise the state, and planned to bring Yang Yi into the regency as well.

sentences.zh: 已而謀泄，罷為太子太傅，封萊國公。

translations.literal: Before long the plot leaked. He was dismissed and made Grand Preceptor of the Crown Prince, enfeoffed as Duke of the State of Lai.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the plot leaked. He was removed as chancellor, appointed Grand Preceptor of the Crown Prince, and enfeoffed as Duke of Lai.

sentences.zh: 時懷政反側不自安，且憂得罪，乃謀殺大臣，請罷皇后預政，奉帝為太上皇，而傳位太子，復相準。

translations.literal: At that time Huaizheng was restless and ill at ease, also fearing punishment. He thereupon plotted to kill great ministers, requested dismissal of the empress's participation in government, installed the Emperor as Retired Emperor, transferred the throne to the Crown Prince, and restored Zhun as chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Huaizheng, restless and fearing punishment, plotted to kill senior ministers, strip the empress of her role in governance, declare the Emperor retired, transfer the throne to the Crown Prince, and restore Kou Zhun as chancellor.

sentences.zh: 客省使楊崇勳等以告丁謂，謂微服夜乘犢車詣曹利用計事，明日以聞。

translations.literal: Reception Corps commissioner Yang Chongxun and others reported this to Ding Wei. Wei went in plain dress at night and rode a calf cart to Cao Liyong to plan affairs; the next day he reported it.
translations.idiomatic: Reception Corps commissioner Yang Chongxun and others informed Ding Wei, who went in disguise by night in a calf cart to consult Cao Liyong; the next day he reported the matter to the throne.

sentences.zh: 乃誅懷政，降準為太常卿、知相州，徙安州，貶道州司馬。

translations.literal: Huaizheng was thereupon executed. Zhun was demoted to Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and prefect of Xiangzhou, transferred to Anzhou, banished as militia officer of Daozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Huaizheng was executed. Kou Zhun was demoted to Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and prefect of Xiangzhou, transferred to Anzhou, and finally banished as militia officer of Daozhou.

sentences.zh: 帝初不知也，他日，問左右曰：「吾目中久不見寇準，何也？」

translations.literal: The Emperor at first did not know. Another day he asked attendants: "In my eyes I have long not seen Kou Zhun — why?"
translations.idiomatic: At first the Emperor knew nothing of this. One day he asked his attendants, "I have not seen Kou Zhun in some time — why is that?"

sentences.zh: 左右莫敢對。

translations.literal: Attendants dared not answer.
translations.idiomatic: None of his attendants dared reply.

sentences.zh: 帝崩時亦信惟準與李迪可託，其見重如此。

translations.literal: When the Emperor died he also trusted that only Zhun and Li Di could be entrusted — such was the regard in which he was held.
translations.idiomatic: Even at his death the Emperor believed that only Kou Zhun and Li Di were fit to be entrusted with the realm — such was the esteem in which he was held.

sentences.zh: 乾興元年，再貶雷州司戶參軍。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianxing he was again banished as registrar of Leizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Qianxing he was banished again, to the post of registrar of Leizhou.

sentences.zh: 初，丁謂出準門至參政，事準甚謹。

translations.literal: Initially, Ding Wei, having risen from Zhun's gate to participation in government, served Zhun very deferentially.
translations.idiomatic: In the beginning Ding Wei had risen through Kou Zhun's patronage to high office and served him with great deference.

sentences.zh: 嘗會食中書，羹污準須，謂起，徐拂之。

translations.literal: Once at a meal in the Secretariat, soup soiled Zhun's beard. Wei rose and slowly brushed it off.
translations.idiomatic: Once at a banquet in the Secretariat, soup splashed on Kou Zhun's beard. Ding Wei rose and gently wiped it clean.

sentences.zh: 準笑曰：「參政國之大臣，乃為官長拂鬚邪？」

translations.literal: Zhun laughed and said: "Grand Councillor, you are a great minister of the state — yet you brush your superior's beard?"
translations.idiomatic: Kou Zhun laughed and said, "Grand Councillor, you are a minister of state — and you wipe your superior's beard?"

sentences.zh: 謂甚愧之，由是傾構日深。

translations.literal: Wei was deeply shamed, and from this plotting to undermine grew daily deeper.
translations.idiomatic: Ding Wei was deeply humiliated, and from that day his intrigues against Kou Zhun grew ever deeper.

sentences.zh: 及準貶未幾，謂亦南竄，道雷州，準遣人以一蒸羊逆境上。

translations.literal: When Zhun was banished, not long afterward Wei was also sent south in exile. Passing Leizhou, Zhun sent a man with one steamed sheep to meet him on the road.
translations.idiomatic: Not long after Kou Zhun's banishment, Ding Wei too was exiled to the south. When he passed Leizhou, Kou Zhun sent a man to meet him on the road with a gift of steamed mutton.

sentences.zh: 謂欲見準，準拒絕之。

translations.literal: Wei wished to see Zhun; Zhun refused.
translations.idiomatic: Ding Wei wished to see Kou Zhun, but Kou Zhun refused.

sentences.zh: 聞家僮謀欲報讎者，乃杜門使縱博，毋得出，伺謂行遠，乃罷。

translations.literal: Hearing household servants plotted revenge, he shut doors and had them gamble freely, not permitted to go out; he waited until Wei had traveled far, then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that his servants plotted revenge, he kept them indoors gambling and forbade them to leave until Ding Wei was far away.

sentences.zh: 天聖元年，徙衡州司馬。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tiansheng he was transferred as militia officer of Hengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tiansheng he was transferred to the post of militia officer of Hengzhou.

sentences.zh: 初，太宗嘗得通天犀，命工為二帶，一以賜準。

translations.literal: Initially, Taizong had once obtained sky-piercing rhinoceros horn and ordered craftsmen to make two belts, one of which he bestowed on Zhun.
translations.idiomatic: Long ago, Emperor Taizong had obtained a piece of sky-piercing rhinoceros horn and had craftsmen fashion two belts, one of which he gave to Kou Zhun.

sentences.zh: 及是，準遣人取自洛中，既至數日，沐浴，具朝服束帶，北面再拜，呼左右趣設臥具，就榻而卒。

translations.literal: At this time Zhun sent someone to fetch it from Luoyang. Several days after it arrived, he bathed, prepared court robes and belt, bowed twice facing north, called attendants to hurry and set bedding, lay down upon the couch and died.
translations.idiomatic: At this point Kou Zhun sent for the belt from Luoyang. A few days after it arrived he bathed, donned court robes and girded himself with the belt, bowed twice facing north, called for his bed to be made, lay down, and died.

sentences.zh: 初，張詠在成都，聞準入相，謂其僚屬曰：「寇公奇材，惜學術不足爾。」

translations.literal: Initially, Zhang Yong was in Chengdu. When he heard Zhun had entered the chancellorship, he said to his staff: "Lord Kou is a remarkable talent — it is a pity his learning is insufficient, that is all."
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Yong was in Chengdu and heard that Kou Zhun had become chancellor, he told his staff, "Lord Kou is a rare talent — it is only a pity his learning is not quite equal to it."

sentences.zh: 及準出陝，詠適自成都罷還，準嚴供帳，大為具待。

translations.literal: When Zhun left Shaanzhou, Yong happened to be returning dismissed from Chengdu. Zhun strictly prepared provisions and greatly entertained him.
translations.idiomatic: When Kou Zhun left his post in Shaanzhou, Zhang Yong happened to be returning dismissed from Chengdu. Kou Zhun prepared a lavish welcome and entertained him generously.

sentences.zh: 詠將去，準送之郊，問曰：「何以教準？」

translations.literal: When Yong was about to depart, Zhun escorted him to the suburbs and asked: "By what might you instruct Zhun?"
translations.idiomatic: As Zhang Yong prepared to leave, Kou Zhun escorted him to the outskirts and asked, "What counsel do you have for me?"

sentences.zh: 詠徐曰：「《霍光傳》不可不讀也。」

translations.literal: Yong said slowly: "The biography of Huo Guang — one cannot fail to read it."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yong replied slowly, "You must read the biography of Huo Guang."

sentences.zh: 準莫諭其意，歸取其傳讀之，至「不學無術」，笑曰：「此張公謂我矣。」

translations.literal: Zhun did not grasp his meaning. Returning he took the biography and read it. When he came to "without learning and without method," he laughed and said: "This is what Lord Zhang meant about me."
translations.idiomatic: Kou Zhun did not grasp his meaning. When he returned home he read the biography and, coming to the phrase "lacking learning and lacking method," laughed and said, "That is what Lord Zhang meant about me."

sentences.zh: 準少年富貴，性豪侈，喜劇飲，每宴賓客，多闔扉脫驂。

translations.literal: Zhun in youth was rich and noble; by nature extravagant, fond of heavy drinking. Whenever he entertained guests, he often shut doors and removed shafts from horses.
translations.idiomatic: Kou Zhun rose to wealth and rank while still young; extravagant by nature, he loved heavy drinking. When he entertained guests he often barred the doors and had the horses unhitched from their carriages so none could leave.

sentences.zh: 家未嘗爇油燈，雖庖匽所在，必然炬燭。

translations.literal: In his household they never lit oil lamps; even where kitchens and privies were, there were invariably torch candles.
translations.idiomatic: His household never used oil lamps — even kitchens and privies were always lit by wax candles.

sentences.zh: 在雷州逾年。

translations.literal: He was in Leizhou for more than a year.
translations.idiomatic: He spent more than a year in Leizhou.

sentences.zh: 既卒，衡州之命乃至，遂歸葬西京。

translations.literal: After he died, the Hengzhou order only then arrived; he was thereupon returned and buried in the Western Capital.
translations.idiomatic: After his death the order transferring him to Hengzhou only then arrived; his body was returned and buried in the Western Capital.

sentences.zh: 道出荊南公安，縣人皆設祭哭於路，折竹植地，掛紙錢，逾月視之，枯竹盡生筍。

translations.literal: The route passed Gong'an in Jingnan. County people all set offerings and wept in the road, broke bamboo and planted it in the ground, hung paper money; after more than a month when they looked, withered bamboo had all sprouted shoots.
translations.idiomatic: When the procession passed through Gong'an in Jingnan, the local people wept along the road and set out offerings. They planted bamboo stakes hung with paper money; more than a month later, every withered stalk had sprouted new shoots.

sentences.zh: 眾因為立廟，歲時享之。

translations.literal: The multitude therefore erected a temple and annually offered sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: The people therefore built him a temple and offered seasonal sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 無子，以從子隨為嗣。

translations.literal: He had no son; he took his nephew Sui as heir.
translations.idiomatic: He had no son and adopted his nephew Sui as his heir.

sentences.zh: 準歿後十一年，復太子太傅，贈中書令、萊國公，後又賜諡曰忠愍。

translations.literal: Eleven years after Zhun's death he was restored as Grand Preceptor of the Crown Prince, posthumously given Director of the Secretariat and Duke of the State of Lai, and later granted posthumous title Loyal and Lamented.
translations.idiomatic: Eleven years after Kou Zhun's death he was reinstated as Grand Preceptor of the Crown Prince, posthumously ennobled as Director of the Secretariat and Duke of Lai, and later granted the posthumous name Loyal and Lamented.

sentences.zh: 皇祐四年，詔翰林學士孫抃撰神道碑，帝為篆其首曰「旌忠」。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Huangyou, an edict ordered Hanlin Academician Sun Bian to compose the spirit-way stele; the Emperor personally seal-scripted its head, reading "In Praise of Loyalty."
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Huangyou, the court ordered Hanlin Academician Sun Bian to compose his spirit-way stele; the Emperor personally inscribed the heading in seal script: "In Praise of Loyalty."

sentences.zh: 論曰：呂端諫秦王居留，表表已見大器，與寇準同相而常讓之，留李繼遷之母不誅。

translations.literal: Discussion says: Lu Duan remonstrated against the Prince of Qin's prolonged stay; his outstanding stature already showed great capacity. Serving as chancellor alongside Kou Zhun he often yielded to him. He spared Li Jiqian's mother from execution.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: Lu Duan remonstrated against Prince Qin's prolonged stay — even then his greatness was evident. As Kou Zhun's fellow chancellor he often deferred to him, and he spared Li Jiqian's mother from execution.

sentences.zh: 真宗之立，閉王繼恩於室，以折李后異謀，而定大計；

translations.literal: In establishing Zhenzong, he shut Wang Jien in a room to break Empress Li's divergent plot and settled the great plan;
translations.idiomatic: In securing Zhenzong's succession he confined Wang Jien to break Empress Li's conspiracy and settle the dynasty's course;

sentences.zh: 既立，猶請去簾，升殿審視，然後下拜，太宗謂之「大事不糊塗」者，知臣莫過君矣。

translations.literal: After establishment, he still requested removal of the screen, ascended the hall to examine closely, then bowed. Taizong called him one who "is not muddled on great matters" — nowhere does understanding ministers surpass the lord.
translations.idiomatic: After the investiture he still insisted the curtain be lifted so he could see the new emperor clearly before bowing. Taizong called him a man who "never muddles great affairs" — truly, no ruler ever knew his ministers better.

sentences.zh: 宰相不和，不足以定大計。

translations.literal: If chancellors are not harmonious, it is insufficient to settle great plans.
translations.idiomatic: Without harmony among chancellors, great affairs cannot be settled.

sentences.zh: 畢士安薦寇準，又為之辨誣。

translations.literal: Bi Shi'an recommended Kou Zhun and also cleared slanders for him.
translations.idiomatic: Bi Shi'an recommended Kou Zhun and defended him against slander.

sentences.zh: 契丹大舉而入，合辭以勸真宗，遂幸澶淵，終卻鉅敵。

translations.literal: When the Khitan entered in force, they united in argument to urge Zhenzong, and he thereupon proceeded to Chanyuan, ultimately repelling the great enemy.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan invaded in force they jointly urged Zhenzong forward, and he proceeded to Chanyuan and ultimately drove back the great enemy.

sentences.zh: 及議歲幣，因請重賄，要其久盟；

translations.literal: When negotiating annual tribute, he thereby requested heavy bribes to exact a long-lasting alliance;
translations.idiomatic: In negotiating the annual tribute he demanded heavy payments to secure a lasting peace;

sentences.zh: 由是西夏失牽制之謀，隨亦內附。

translations.literal: By this Western Xia lost its plan to tie them down, and accordingly also submitted internally.
translations.idiomatic: thereby depriving Western Xia of its leverage, which soon submitted as well.

sentences.zh: 景德、咸平以來，天下乂安，二相協和之所致也。

translations.literal: From Jingde and Xianping onward, the realm was governed in peace — this was brought about by the two chancellors' harmony.
translations.idiomatic: From the Jingde and Xianping eras onward the realm enjoyed peace — the fruit of harmony between the two chancellors.

sentences.zh: 準於太宗朝論建太子，謂神器不可謀及婦人、謀及中官、謀及近臣。

translations.literal: Zhun, in Taizong's court when discussing establishment of the Crown Prince, said the divine vessel must not be plotted over involving women, involving palace eunuchs, or involving close ministers.
translations.idiomatic: In Taizong's reign Kou Zhun argued for naming the Crown Prince, declaring that the succession must never be decided with women, eunuchs, or favored courtiers.

sentences.zh: 此三言者，可為萬世龜鑒。

translations.literal: These three statements may serve as tortoise-and-mirror for ten thousand generations.
translations.idiomatic: These three warnings should be mirrors for all generations to come.

sentences.zh: 澶淵之幸，力沮眾議，竟成雋功，古所謂大臣者，於斯見之。

translations.literal: At the Chanyuan expedition he forcefully checked the multitude's opinions and in the end achieved outstanding merit — the great ministers of antiquity, it is said, are seen in this.
translations.idiomatic: At Chanyuan he forcefully held back the court's wavering counsels and in the end won a signal achievement — in him one sees what the ancients meant by a great minister.

sentences.zh: 然挽衣留諫，面詆同列，雖有直言之風，而少包荒之量。

translations.literal: Yet seizing robes to detain and remonstrate, and reviling colleagues to their faces — though he had the spirit of blunt speech, he lacked the breadth to encompass wrongdoing.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he seized colleagues by the robe to detain them in argument and reviled his peers to their faces. Though he had the spirit of blunt speech, he lacked the magnanimity to bear with others' faults.

sentences.zh: 定策禁中，不慎所與，致啟懷政邪謀，坐竄南裔。

translations.literal: In fixing policy within the palace he was not careful whom he associated with, which led to the rise of Huai Zheng's wicked plot, and he was banished to the southern marches on that account.
translations.idiomatic: In settling policy within the palace he was careless in his associates, which opened the way for Zhou Huaizheng's treacherous scheme and led to his exile in the far south.

sentences.zh: 勳業如是而不令厥終，所謂「臣不密則失身」，豈不信哉！

translations.literal: Merit and achievement such as his yet not granted a good end — what is called "if the minister is not discreet he loses his person" — is this not truly so!
translations.idiomatic: Merit such as his yet no fair end — truly, as the saying goes, "when the minister is not discreet, he loses his person." Can one doubt it?
